texts.label: text
texts.orig: For more than 50 years, ISACA® (www.isaca.org) has advanced the best talent, expertise and learning in technology. ISACA equips individuals with knowledge, credentials, education and community to progress their careers and transform their organizations, and enables enterprises to train and build quality teams. Among those credentials, ISACA advances and validates business-critical skills and knowledge through the globally respected Certified Information Systems Auditor® (CISA®), Certified in Risk and Information Systems Control® (CRISC®), Certified Information Security Manager® (CISM®), Certified in the Governance of Enterprise IT® (CGEIT®) and Certified Data Privacy Solutions Engineer™ (CDPSE™) credentials. ISACA is a global professional association and learning organization that leverages the expertise of its 145,000 members who work in information security, governance, assurance, risk and privacy to drive innovation through technology. It has a presence in 188 countries, including more than 220 chapters worldwide.

texts.orig: ISACA is pleased to offer the 1,000 questions in this CISM® Review Questions, Answers & Explanations Manual 10th Edition. The purpose of this manual is to provide the CISM candidate with sample questions and testing topics to help prepare and study for the CISM exam.
texts.text: ISACA is pleased to offer the 1,000 questions in this CISM® Review Questions, Answers & Explanations Manual 10th Edition. The purpose of this manual is to provide the CISM candidate with sample questions and testing topics to help prepare and study for the CISM exam.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: This manual consists of 1,000 multiple-choice study questions, answers and explanations, which are organized according to the newly revised (effective 2022) CISM job practice domains. These questions, answers and explanations are intended to introduce CISM candidates to the types of questions that may appear on the CISM exam. They are not actual questions from the exam. Some of these itemis appeared in previous editions of the CISM® Review Questions, Answers & Explanations Manual, but many have been rewritten or enhanced to be more representative of actual exam items and to provide further clarity or reflect a change in practice. The 1,000 questions are sorted by CISM domains. Additionally, 150 questions have been extracted to provide a sample exam with quesțions in the same proportion as the current CISM job practice. The candidate also may want to obtain a copy of the CISM® Review Manual 16th Edition, which provides the foundational knowledge of a CISM.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The CISM exam evaluates a candidate's practical knowledge, including experience and application, of the job practice domains. We recommend that the exam candidate look to multiple resources to prepare for the exam, including the CISM® Review Manual and Questions, Answers & Explanation (QAE) Manual or the database, along with external publications. This section will cover some tips for studying for the exam and how best to use this QAE Manual in conjunction with other resources.

We recommend that the exam candidate look to multiple resources to prepare for the exam, including the CISM® Review Manual and Questions, Answers & Explanation (QAE) Manual or the database, along with external publications. texts.orig: GETTING STARTED
texts.text: GETTING STARTED

texts.label: text
texts.orig: Having adequate time to prepare for the CISM exam is critical. Most candidates spend between three and six months studying prior to taking the exam. Make sure you set aside a designated time each week to study, which you may wish to increase as your exam date approaches.
texts.text: Having adequate time to prepare for the CISM exam is critical. Most candidates spend between three and six months studying prior to taking the exam. Make sure you set aside a designated time each week to study, which you may wish to increase as your exam date approaches.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: CISM exam questions are developed with the intent of measuring and testing practical knowledge and the application of information security managerial principles and standards. All questions are presented in a multiplechoice format and are designed for one best answer.
texts.text: CISM exam questions are developed with the intent of measuring and testing practical knowledge and the application of information security managerial principles and standards. All questions are presented in a multiplechoice format and are designed for one best answer.

texts.label: text
texts.orig: The candidate is cautioned to read each question carefully. Many times a CISM exam question will require the candidate to choose the appropriate answer that is MOST likely or BEST, or the candidate may be asked to choose a practice or procedure that would be performed FIRST related to the other answers. In every case, the candidate is required to read the question carefully, eliminate known wrong answers and then make the best choice possible. Knowing that these types of questions are asked and how to study for them will go a long way toward answering them correctly. The best answer is one of the choices provided. There can be many potential solutions to the scenarios posed in the questions, depending on industry, geographical location, etc. It is advisable to consider the information provided in the question and to determine the best answer of the options provided.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 1. Which of the following is the MOST effective way to ensure that noncompliance to information security standards is resolved?
texts.text: Which of the following is the MOST effective way to ensure that noncompliance to information security standards is resolved?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Periodic audits of noncompliant areas
texts.text: Periodic audits of noncompliant areas

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. An ongoing vulnerability scanning program
texts.text: An ongoing vulnerability scanning program

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Regular reports to the audit committee
texts.text: Regular reports to the audit committee

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Annual security awareness training
texts.text: Annual security awareness training

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Periodic audits can be effective but only when combined with reporting.
texts.text: Periodic audits can be effective but only when combined with reporting.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Training can increase management's awareness regarding information security, but awareness training is generally not as compelling to management as having individual names highlighted on a compliance report.
texts.text: Training can increase management's awareness regarding information security, but awareness training is generally not as compelling to management as having individual names highlighted on a compliance report.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Vulnerability scanning has little to do with noncompliance with standards.
texts.text: Vulnerability scanning has little to do with noncompliance with standards.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Reporting noncompliance to the audit committee is the most effective way to have enforcement for concerned parties to take the proper action in order to comply.
texts.text: Reporting noncompliance to the audit committee is the most effective way to have enforcement for concerned parties to take the proper action in order to comply.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 2. Senior management commitment and support for information security can BEST be obtained through presentations that:
texts.text: Senior management commitment and support for information security can BEST be obtained through presentations that:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. use illustrative examples of successful attacks.
texts.text: use illustrative examples of successful attacks.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. explain the technical risk to the enterprise.
texts.text: explain the technical risk to the enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. evaluate the enterprise against good security practices.
texts.text: evaluate the enterprise against good security practices.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. tie security risk to key business objectives.
texts.text: tie security risk to key business objectives.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Senior management may not be as interested in examples of successful attacks if they are not tied to the impact on business environment and objectives.
texts.text: Senior management may not be as interested in examples of successful attacks if they are not tied to the impact on business environment and objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: on business environment and objectives.
texts.text: on business environment and objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Tying security risk to key business objectives is the best option to obtain senior managers' commitment and support as they want to understand the justification for investing in security in relation to achieving key business objectives.
texts.text: Tying security risk to key business objectives is the best option to obtain senior managers' commitment and support as they want to understand the justification for investing in security in relation to achieving key business objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Industry good practices may be important to senior management to the extent they are relevant to the enterprise and its business objectives; however, this is not the best method of gaining commitment and support for information security.
texts.text: Industry good practices may be important to senior management to the extent they are relevant to the enterprise and its business objectives; however, this is not the best method of gaining commitment and support for information security.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 3. The MOST appropriate role for senior management in supporting information security is the:
texts.text: The MOST appropriate role for senior management in supporting information security is the:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. evaluation of vendors offering security products.
texts.text: evaluation of vendors offering security products.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. assessment of risk to the enterprise.
texts.text: assessment of risk to the enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. approval of policy statements and funding.
texts.text: approval of policy statements and funding.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. developing standards sufficient to achieve acceptable risk.
texts.text: developing standards sufficient to achieve acceptable risk.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Evaluation of vendors is the responsibility of the information security manager; however, this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security. Senior management may be involved in vendor evaluation in some enterprises, but its primary role is in setting the enterprise's business direction, oversight and governance.
texts.text: Evaluation of vendors is the responsibility of the information security manager; however, this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security. Senior management may be involved in vendor evaluation in some enterprises, but its primary role is in setting the enterprise's business direction, oversight and governance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Assessment of risk is the responsibility of the information security manager and this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security.
texts.text: Assessment of risk is the responsibility of the information security manager and this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Policies are a statement of senior management intent and direction that should be approved by senior management. It should also provide sufficient funding to achieve the enterprise's information security objectives. This is the most appropriate role for senior management in supporting information security,
texts.text: Policies are a statement of senior management intent and direction that should be approved by senior management. It should also provide sufficient funding to achieve the enterprise's information security objectives. This is the most appropriate role for senior management in supporting information security,

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The development of standards that meet the policy intent is typically a function of the information security manager and this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security.
texts.text: The development of standards that meet the policy intent is typically a function of the information security manager and this is not a role for senior management in supporting information security.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 4. Which of the following would be the BEST indicator of effective information security governance within an enterprise?
texts.text: Which of the following would be the BEST indicator of effective information security governance within an enterprise?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The steering committee approves security projects.
texts.text: The steering committee approves security projects.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Security policy training is provided to all managers.
texts.text: Security policy training is provided to all managers.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Security training is available to all employees on the intranet.
texts.text: Security training is available to all employees on the intranet.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. IT personnel are trained in testing and applying required patches.
texts.text: IT personnel are trained in testing and applying required patches.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The existence of a steering committee that approves all security projects is the best indicator of an effective governance program. To ensure that all stakeholders impacted by security considerations are involved, many enterprises use a steering committee comprised of senior representatives of affected groups. This composition helps to achieve consensus on priorities and trade-offs and serves as an effective communication channel for ensuring the alignment of the security program with business objectives,
texts.text: The existence of a steering committee that approves all security projects is the best indicator of an effective governance program. To ensure that all stakeholders impacted by security considerations are involved, many enterprises use a steering committee comprised of senior representatives of affected groups. This composition helps to achieve consensus on priorities and trade-offs and serves as an effective communication channel for ensuring the alignment of the security program with business objectives,

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Security policy training for all managers is important at all levels of the enterprise but it is not the best indicator of effective governance. The training program should be guided and approved as a security project by the steering committee.
texts.text: Security policy training for all managers is important at all levels of the enterprise but it is not the best indicator of effective governance. The training program should be guided and approved as a security project by the steering committee.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The availability of security training to all over the intranet, while beneficial to the overall security program, is not the best indicator of effective governance, as it is an operational activity in information security. Security training should be guided and approved as a security project by the steering committee.
texts.text: The availability of security training to all over the intranet, while beneficial to the overall security program, is not the best indicator of effective governance, as it is an operational activity in information security. Security training should be guided and approved as a security project by the steering committee.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Even enterprises with little overall governance may be effective in patching systems in a timely manner; this is not the best indicator of effective governance. Testing and applying patches is an operational activity in information security and not part of governance.
texts.text: Even enterprises with little overall governance may be effective in patching systems in a timely manner; this is not the best indicator of effective governance. Testing and applying patches is an operational activity in information security and not part of governance.

A newly appointed information security manager has been asked to redefine information security requirements because senior management is unhappy with the current state of information security. Which of the following choices would the information security manager consider MOST critical?
texts.text: A newly appointed information security manager has been asked to redefine information security requirements because senior management is unhappy with the current state of information security. Which of the following choices would the information security manager consider MOST critical?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The business strategy
texts.text: The business strategy

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. User competencies

texts.orig: A. Industry frameworks are useful in improving security implementation to the extent that they align with and support business objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Security requirements are driven by the information security policy, procedures and practices. texts.orig: 55. Management requests that an information security manager determine which regulations regarding disclosure, reporting and privacy are the most important for the enterprise to address. The recommendations for addressing these legal and regulatory requirements will be MOST useful if based on which of the following choices?
texts.text: Management requests that an information security manager determine which regulations regarding disclosure, reporting and privacy are the most important for the enterprise to address. The recommendations for addressing these legal and regulatory requirements will be MOST useful if based on which of the following choices?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The extent of enforcement actions
texts.text: The extent of enforcement actions

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The probability and consequences
texts.text: The probability and consequences

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The sanctions for noncompliance
texts.text: The sanctions for noncompliance

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The amount of personal liability
texts.text: The amount of personal liability

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The extent of enforcement is a measure of probability. Without knowing the scope of consequences, probability cannot be viewed in context.
texts.text: The extent of enforcement is a measure of probability. Without knowing the scope of consequences, probability cannot be viewed in context.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Legal and regulatory requirements should be treated as any other risk to the enterprise, calculated as the probability of enforcement and the magnitude of possible sanctions (impact or consequences).
texts.text: Legal and regulatory requirements should be treated as any other risk to the enterprise, calculated as the probability of enforcement and the magnitude of possible sanctions (impact or consequences).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Sanctions or impact must be considered in the context of the enforcement mechanisms. If sanctions have less probability of being implemented due to lax enforcement, their severity poses lower risk to the enterprise than if they are widely enforced.
texts.text: Sanctions or impact must be considered in the context of the enforcement mechanisms. If sanctions have less probability of being implemented due to lax enforcement, their severity poses lower risk to the enterprise than if they are widely enforced.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Except in extreme cases of fraud or other criminal activity, liability for regulatory sanctions generally lies with senior management and the board of directors. It is not a driving factor in the evaluation of regulatory requirements.
texts.text: Except in extreme cases of fraud or other criminal activity, liability for regulatory sanctions generally lies with senior management and the board of directors. It is not a driving factor in the evaluation of regulatory requirements.

texts.orig: 56. How should an information security manager balance the potentially conflicting requirements of an international enterprise's security standards with local regulation?
texts.text: How should an information security manager balance the potentially conflicting requirements of an international enterprise's security standards with local regulation?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Give organizational standards preference over local regulations.
texts.text: Give organizational standards preference over local regulations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Follow local regulations only.
texts.text: Follow local regulations only.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Make the enterprise aware of those standards where local regulations cause conflicts.
texts.text: Make the enterprise aware of those standards where local regulations cause conflicts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Negotiate a local version of the enterprise standards.
texts.text: Negotiate a local version of the enterprise standards.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Organizational standards must be subordinate to local regulations.
texts.text: Organizational standards must be subordinate to local regulations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. It would be incorrect to follow local regulations only, because there must be recognition of organizational requirements.
texts.text: It would be incorrect to follow local regulations only, because there must be recognition of organizational requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Making an enterprise aware of standards is a sensible step but is not a complete solution.
texts.text: Making an enterprise aware of standards is a sensible step but is not a complete solution.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Negotiating a local version of the enterprise's standards is the most effective compromise in this situation. Regulations cannot be changed by the enterprise, and it must achieve compliance, making it necessary to develop a local version of its standards in consultation with the principal office.
texts.text: Negotiating a local version of the enterprise's standards is the most effective compromise in this situation. Regulations cannot be changed by the enterprise, and it must achieve compliance, making it necessary to develop a local version of its standards in consultation with the principal office.

texts.orig: 64. Which of the following choices is the MOST likely cause of significant inconsistencies in system configurations?
texts.text: Which of the following choices is the MOST likely cause of significant inconsistencies in system configurations?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A lack of procedures
texts.text: A lack of procedures

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Inadequate governance
texts.text: Inadequate governance

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Poor standards
texts.text: Poor standards

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Insufficient training
texts.text: Insufficient training

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A lack of proper procedures is a failure of governance and may be a cause of significant inconsistencies in system configurations; however, it is not the most likely one. Governance takes precedence, as it has to be in place to ensure proper procedures.
texts.text: A lack of proper procedures is a failure of governance and may be a cause of significant inconsistencies in system configurations; however, it is not the most likely one. Governance takes precedence, as it has to be in place to ensure proper procedures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Governance includes the set of rules the enterprise operates by, oversight to ensure compliance, and feedback mechanisms that provide assurance the rules are followed. A failure of one or more of these processes is most likely to be the reason for inconsistencies in system configurations.
texts.text: Governance includes the set of rules the enterprise operates by, oversight to ensure compliance, and feedback mechanisms that provide assurance the rules are followed. A failure of one or more of these processes is most likely to be the reason for inconsistencies in system configurations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Poor standards are a sign of inadequate governance and may result in inconsistencies in system configurations; however, this is not the most likely reason, as governance takes precedence.
texts.text: Poor standards are a sign of inadequate governance and may result in inconsistencies in system configurations; however, this is not the most likely reason, as governance takes precedence.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Insufficient training indicates that there are no requirements, or that the requirements are not being met, or that the trainers are not competent in the subject matter, all of which reflect ineffective governance that can result in a lack of oversight, a lack of clear requirements for training, or a lack of suitable metrics.
texts.text: Insufficient training indicates that there are no requirements, or that the requirements are not being met, or that the trainers are not competent in the subject matter, all of which reflect ineffective governance that can result in a lack of oversight, a lack of clear requirements for training, or a lack of suitable metrics.

texts.orig: 69. Which of the following elements is MOST important when developing an information security strategy?
texts.text: Which of the following elements is MOST important when developing an information security strategy?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Defined objectives
texts.text: Defined objectives

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Time frames for delivery
texts.text: Time frames for delivery

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Adoption of a control framework
texts.text: Adoption of a control framework

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Without defined objectives, the information security strategy and plan to achieve objectives cannot be developed, so defined objectives are the most important element.
texts.text: Without defined objectives, the information security strategy and plan to achieve objectives cannot be developed, so defined objectives are the most important element.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 70. Laws and regulations should be addressed by the information security manager:
texts.text: Laws and regulations should be addressed by the information security manager:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. to the extent that they impact the enterprise.
texts.text: to the extent that they impact the enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. by implementing international standards.
texts.text: by implementing international standards.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. by developing policies that address the requirements.
texts.text: by developing policies that address the requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. to ensure that guidelines meet the requirements.
texts.text: to ensure that guidelines meet the requirements.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Legal and regulatory requirements should be assessed based on the extent and nature of enforcement, the probability of enforcement action and sanctions, and the impact of noncompliance or partial compliance balanced against the costs of compliance.
texts.text: Legal and regulatory requirements should be assessed based on the extent and nature of enforcement, the probability of enforcement action and sanctions, and the impact of noncompliance or partial compliance balanced against the costs of compliance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. International standards may not address the legal requirements in question.
texts.text: International standards may not address the legal requirements in question.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Policies should not address particular regulations because regulations are subject to change. Policies should only address the need to assess regulatory requirements and deal with them appropriately based on risk and impact.
texts.text: Policies should not address particular regulations because regulations are subject to change. Policies should only address the need to assess regulatory requirements and deal with them appropriately based on risk and impact.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Guidelines would normally not address regulations, although standards may address regulations based on management's determination of the appropriate level of compliance.
texts.text: Guidelines would normally not address regulations, although standards may address regulations based on management's determination of the appropriate level of compliance.

texts.text: Which of the following actions would help to change an enterprise's security culture?

texts.orig: A. Develop procedures to enforce the information security policy.
texts.text: Develop procedures to enforce the information security policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Obtain strong management support.

texts.text: Implement strict technical security controls.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header

texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Procedures will support an information security policy, but this is not likely to have much impact on the security culture of the enterprise.
texts.text: Procedures will support an information security policy, but this is not likely to have much impact on the security culture of the enterprise.

texts.orig: 78. An enterprise has been recently subject to a series of denial-of-service attacks due to a weakness in security. texts.text: An enterprise has been recently subject to a series of denial-of-service attacks due to a weakness in security. The information security manager needs to present a business case for increasing the investment in security. The MOST significant challenge in obtaining approval from senior management for the proposal is:

texts.label: list_item

texts.orig: A. using a bottom-up approach.
texts.text: using a bottom-up approach.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. management by the IT department.
texts.text: management by the IT department.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. referring the matter to the enterprise's legal department.
texts.text: referring the matter to the enterprise's legal department.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. using a top-down approach.
texts.text: using a top-down approach.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Enterprise security governance may not be reflected effectively by a bottom-up approach, as it will not bring focus to management priorities.
texts.text: Enterprise security governance may not be reflected effectively by a bottom-up approach, as it will not bring focus to management priorities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Governance of enterprise security affects the entire enterprise, not just the management of IT.
texts.text: Governance of enterprise security affects the entire enterprise, not just the management of IT.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The legal department is part of the overall governance process and may provide useful input but cannot take full responsibility.
texts.text: The legal department is part of the overall governance process and may provide useful input but cannot take full responsibility.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Effective governance of enterprise security needs to be a top-down initiative, with the board and executive management setting clear policies, goals and objectives and providing for their ongoing monitoring.
texts.text: Effective governance of enterprise security needs to be a top-down initiative, with the board and executive management setting clear policies, goals and objectives and providing for their ongoing monitoring.

texts.orig: 87. The FIRST step to create an internal culture that embraces information security is to:

texts.orig: 89. After completing a full IT risk assessment, who is in the BEST position to decide which mitigating controls should be implemented?
texts.text: After completing a full IT risk assessment, who is in the BEST position to decide which mitigating controls should be implemented?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Senior management
texts.text: Senior management

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The business manager
texts.text: The business manager

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The IT audit manager
texts.text: The IT audit manager

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The information security officer
texts.text: The information security officer

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Senior management will have to ensure that the business manager has a clear understanding of the risk assessed, but it will not be in a position to decide on specific controls.
texts.text: Senior management will have to ensure that the business manager has a clear understanding of the risk assessed, but it will not be in a position to decide on specific controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The business manager will be in the best position, based on the risk assessment and mitigation proposals, to decide which controls to implement, in line with the business strategy and budget.
texts.text: The business manager will be in the best position, based on the risk assessment and mitigation proposals, to decide which controls to implement, in line with the business strategy and budget.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The IT audit manager will take part in the process of identifying threats and vulnerabilities and make recommendations for mitigation.
texts.text: The IT audit manager will take part in the process of identifying threats and vulnerabilities and make recommendations for mitigation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The information security officer could make some decisions regarding implementation of controls. However, the business manager will have a broader business view and better understanding of control impact on the business goals and, therefore, will be in a better position to make strategic decisions.
texts.text: The information security officer could make some decisions regarding implementation of controls. However, the business manager will have a broader business view and better understanding of control impact on the business goals and, therefore, will be in a better position to make strategic decisions.

texts.orig: 90. Of the following, which is the MOST effective way to measure enterprise alignment of an information security program?
texts.text: Of the following, which is the MOST effective way to measure enterprise alignment of an information security program?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Track audits over time.
texts.text: Track audits over time.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Evaluate incident losses.
texts.text: Evaluate incident losses.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Analyze business cases.
texts.text: Analyze business cases.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Interview business owners.
texts.text: Interview business owners.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Audit reports may indicate areas of security activity that do not optimally support the enterprise objectives, but they will not be as good an indicator as insight from business owners.
texts.text: Audit reports may indicate areas of security activity that do not optimally support the enterprise objectives, but they will not be as good an indicator as insight from business owners.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Losses may or may not be considered acceptable by the enterprise but will not be well correlated with the perception of business support.
texts.text: Losses may or may not be considered acceptable by the enterprise but will not be well correlated with the perception of business support.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. To the extent that business cases have been developed for particular security activities, they will be a good indication of how well business requirements were considered; however, the perception of business owners will ultimately be the most important factor.
texts.text: To the extent that business cases have been developed for particular security activities, they will be a good indication of how well business requirements were considered; however, the perception of business owners will ultimately be the most important factor.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. It is essential that business owners understand and support the security program and fully understand how its controls impact their activities. This can be most readily accomplished through direct interaction with business leadership.
texts.text: It is essential that business owners understand and support the security program and fully understand how its controls impact their activities. This can be most readily accomplished through direct interaction with business leadership.

texts.orig: 91. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate as a mcans of obtaining commitment from senior management for implementation of the information security strategy?
texts.text: Which of the following is the MOST appropriate as a mcans of obtaining commitment from senior management for implementation of the information security strategy?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Educational material discussing the importance of good information security practices
texts.text: Educational material discussing the importance of good information security practices

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Regular group meetings to review the challenges and requirements of daily operations
texts.text: Regular group meetings to review the challenges and requirements of daily operations

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A cost-benefit analysis detailing how the requested implementation budget will be used
texts.text: A cost-benefit analysis detailing how the requested implementation budget will be used

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: A formal presentation highlighting the relationship between security and business goals

texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Education regarding good information security practices is a part of implementing an effective information security program and is best distributed across the workforce.
texts.text: Education regarding good information security practices is a part of implementing an effective information security program and is best distributed across the workforce.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Senior managers are unlikely to be able to accommodate regular group meetings, and daily operations are better addressed at the level of business process owners.
texts.text: Senior managers are unlikely to be able to accommodate regular group meetings, and daily operations are better addressed at the level of business process owners.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A detailed cost-benefit analysis of the implementation budget is a supporting document that can be referenced to answer questions and establish credibility.: However, as a stand-alone document it is not the means by which an information security manager obtains commitment from senior management to implement the information security strategy.
texts.text: A detailed cost-benefit analysis of the implementation budget is a supporting document that can be referenced to answer questions and establish credibility.: However, as a stand-alone document it is not the means by which an information security manager obtains commitment from senior management to implement the information security strategy.

texts.orig: D. A formal presentation to senior management is most appropriate to obtain management commitment when used as a means to educate and communicate key aspects of the overall security program and how security is enabling the achievement of business goals.
texts.text: A formal presentation to senior management is most appropriate to obtain management commitment when used as a means to educate and communicate key aspects of the overall security program and how security is enabling the achievement of business goals.

texts.orig: 92. Which of the following BEST describes the key objective of an information security program?
texts.text: Which of the following BEST describes the key objective of an information security program?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Achieve strategic business goals and objectives.
texts.text: Achieve strategic business goals and objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Establish accountability for information security risk
texts.text: Establish accountability for information security risk

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Establish ownership of information security risk

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Eliminate threats to the enterprise.

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: While the activities of the security program are primarily concerned with protection of the enterprise?s assets, the key objective is to support the achievement of the strategic business goals and objectives.
texts.text: While the activities of the security program are primarily concerned with protection of the enterprise?s assets, the key objective is to support the achievement of the strategic business goals and objectives.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Information security is achieved by implementing any type of control; it is achieved not just by using IT controls, but also by using manual controls.

texts.text: An information security program focuses on protecting information assets using manual and automated controls with the objective of supporting the achievement of strategic business goals.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Threats cannot be eliminated; information security controls help reduce risk to an acceptable level.
texts.text: Threats cannot be eliminated; information security controls help reduce risk to an acceptable level.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Laws and regulations of the country of origin may not be enforceable in the foreign country.
texts.text: Laws and regulations of the country of origin may not be enforceable in the foreign country.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Additional network intrusion detection sensors should be installed, resulting in an additional cost.
texts.text: Additional network intrusion detection sensors should be installed, resulting in an additional cost.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A security breach notification might get delayed due to the time difference.
texts.text: A security breach notification might get delayed due to the time difference.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The company could lose physical control over the server and be unable to monitor the physical security posture of the servers.
texts.text: The company could lose physical control over the server and be unable to monitor the physical security posture of the servers.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A company is held to the local laws and regulations of the country in which thé company resides, even if the company decides to place servers with a vendor that hosts the servers in a foreign country. A potential violation of local laws applicable to the company might not be recognized or rectified (i.e., prosecuted) due to the lack of knowledge of the local laws that are applicable and the inability to enforce the laws.
texts.text: A company is held to the local laws and regulations of the country in which thé company resides, even if the company decides to place servers with a vendor that hosts the servers in a foreign country. A potential violation of local laws applicable to the company might not be recognized or rectified (i.e., prosecuted) due to the lack of knowledge of the local laws that are applicable and the inability to enforce the laws.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Time difference does not play a role in a 24/7 environment. Pagers, cellular phones, telephones, etc., are usually available to communicate notifications.
texts.text: Time difference does not play a role in a 24/7 environment. Pagers, cellular phones, telephones, etc., are usually available to communicate notifications.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Most hosting providers have standardized the level of physical security in place. Regular physical audits can address such concerns.
texts.text: Most hosting providers have standardized the level of physical security in place. Regular physical audits can address such concerns.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Installation of additional network intrusion detection sensors is à manageable problem that requires additional funding but it can be addressed.
texts.text: Installation of additional network intrusion detection sensors is à manageable problem that requires additional funding but it can be addressed.

In an impact analysis, threats to assets are identified and potential business losses determined for different time periods. This assessment is used to justify the extent of safeguards that are required and determine recovery time frames. This analysis is the basis for establishing the recovery strategy.

texts.orig: 112. Which of the following choices is the BEST indicator of the state of information security governance?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A defined maturity level
texts.text: A defined maturity level

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A developed security strategy
texts.text: A developed security strategy

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Complete policies and standards
texts.text: Complete policies and standards

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A defined maturity level is the best overal indicator of the state of information security governance. The maturity level indicates how mature a process is on a scale from 0 (incomplete process) to 5 (optimized process).
texts.text: A defined maturity level is the best overal indicator of the state of information security governance. The maturity level indicates how mature a process is on a scale from 0 (incomplete process) to 5 (optimized process).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A developed security strategy is an important first step, but it must be implemented properly to be effective; by itself, it is not an indication of the state of information security governance.
texts.text: A developed security strategy is an important first step, but it must be implemented properly to be effective; by itself, it is not an indication of the state of information security governance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The number of incidents is relatively unconnected to the effectiveness of information security governance. Trends in incidents would be a better indicator.
texts.text: The number of incidents is relatively unconnected to the effectiveness of information security governance. Trends in incidents would be a better indicator.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Complete policies and standards are required for effective governance but are only one part of the requirement. By themselves, they are not an indicator of the effectiveness of information security governance.
texts.text: Complete policies and standards are required for effective governance but are only one part of the requirement. By themselves, they are not an indicator of the effectiveness of information security governance.

texts.orig: B. Management often considers security to be a financial drain and over-reactive. Showing probable outcomes can help build a case, but demonstrating how the program will materially assist in achieving the desired business outcomes will be more effective.
texts.text: Management often considers security to be a financial drain and over-reactive. Showing probable outcomes can help build a case, but demonstrating how the program will materially assist in achieving the desired business outcomes will be more effective.

texts.orig: 135. Serious-security incidents typically lead to renewed focus on information security by management. To BEST use this attention, the information security manager should make the case for:
texts.text: Serious-security incidents typically lead to renewed focus on information security by management. To BEST use this attention, the information security manager should make the case for:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. improving integration of business and information security processes.
texts.text: improving integration of business and information security processes.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. increasing information security budgets and staffing levels.
texts.text: increasing information security budgets and staffing levels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. developing tighter controls and stronger compliance efforts.
texts.text: developing tighter controls and stronger compliance efforts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. acquiring better supplemental technical security controls.
texts.text: acquiring better supplemental technical security controls.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Close integration of information security governance with overall enterprise governance is likely to provide better long-term security by institutionalizing its activities and increasing visibility in all enterprise activities.
texts.text: Close integration of information security governance with overall enterprise governance is likely to provide better long-term security by institutionalizing its activities and increasing visibility in all enterprise activities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Control strength and compliance efforts must be balanced against business requirements, culture and other enterprise factors that are best accomplished at governance levels.
texts.text: Control strength and compliance efforts must be balanced against business requirements, culture and other enterprise factors that are best accomplished at governance levels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Increased budgets and staff may improve security, but they will not have the same beneficial impact as incorporating security into the strategic levels of the enterprise's operations.
texts.text: Increased budgets and staff may improve security, but they will not have the same beneficial impact as incorporating security into the strategic levels of the enterprise's operations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. While technical security controls may improve some aspects of security, they will not address management issues nor provide enduring changes that are needed for an overall improvement of the enterprise security posture.
texts.text: While technical security controls may improve some aspects of security, they will not address management issues nor provide enduring changes that are needed for an overall improvement of the enterprise security posture.

texts.orig: 160. Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective approach to achieve strategic alignment?
texts.text: Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective approach to achieve strategic alignment?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Periodically survey management
texts.text: Periodically survey management

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Implement a governance framework
texts.text: Implement a governance framework

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Ensure that controls meet objectives
texts.text: Ensure that controls meet objectives

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Develop an enterprise architecture
texts.text: Develop an enterprise architecture

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Achieving and maintaining strategic alignment means that business process owners and managers believe that information security is effectively supporting their organizational activities. This can most easily and inexpensively be determined by periodic surveys, which will also indicate improvement or degradation over time.
texts.text: Achieving and maintaining strategic alignment means that business process owners and managers believe that information security is effectively supporting their organizational activities. This can most easily and inexpensively be determined by periodic surveys, which will also indicate improvement or degradation over time.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Implementing an appropriate governance framework may improve strategic alignment in addition to a number of other benefits, but it is exceedingly complex, time-consuming and expensive and may not directly capture business owners' perceptions or show changes over time.
texts.text: Implementing an appropriate governance framework may improve strategic alignment in addition to a number of other benefits, but it is exceedingly complex, time-consuming and expensive and may not directly capture business owners' perceptions or show changes over time.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. While important, controls meeting objectives may not be perceived by managers as helpful to the business and may, in fact, be seen as an impediment to their activities.
texts.text: While important, controls meeting objectives may not be perceived by managers as helpful to the business and may, in fact, be seen as an impediment to their activities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. An enterprise architecture should consider business objectives during design and development, but in an effort to balance many other requirements, such as security and functionality, it may or may not be perceived as supporting business activities.
texts.text: An enterprise architecture should consider business objectives during design and development, but in an effort to balance many other requirements, such as security and functionality, it may or may not be perceived as supporting business activities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 161. Which of the following is PRIMARILY related to the emergence of governance, risk and compliance?
texts.text: Which of the following is PRIMARILY related to the emergence of governance, risk and compliance?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The increasing need for controls
texts.text: The increasing need for controls

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The policy development process
texts.text: The policy development process

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The integration of assurance-related activities
texts.text: The integration of assurance-related activities

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. A model for information security program development
texts.text: A model for information security program development

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. One of the outcomes of governance, risk and compliance (GRC) is the increased attention on general controls, because they are more pervasive and cost-effective than application-level controls. However, the primary driver for GRC is the increased complexity and diversity of assurance requirements and the need to address them through one integrated process.
texts.text: One of the outcomes of governance, risk and compliance (GRC) is the increased attention on general controls, because they are more pervasive and cost-effective than application-level controls. However, the primary driver for GRC is the increased complexity and diversity of assurance requirements and the need to address them through one integrated process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. As with most information security activities, appropriate policy support is needed for effective GRC implementation, but that is only one aspect of achieving integration.
texts.text: As with most information security activities, appropriate policy support is needed for effective GRC implementation, but that is only one aspect of achieving integration.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. GRC is a process to integrate multiple disparate but related activities to improve effectiveness, reduce or eliminate conflicting approaches, and reduce costs.
texts.text: GRC is a process to integrate multiple disparate but related activities to improve effectiveness, reduce or eliminate conflicting approaches, and reduce costs.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. GRC is not a model, but an approach to achieving greater assurance process integration.
texts.text: GRC is not a model, but an approach to achieving greater assurance process integration.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: a prescriptive methodology for designing the systems architecture.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: a process that ensures alignment with business objectives.

texts.orig: 170. The FIRST action for an information security manager to take when presented with news that new regulations are being applied to how enterprises handle sensitive data is to determine:
texts.text: The FIRST action for an information security manager to take when presented with news that new regulations are being applied to how enterprises handle sensitive data is to determine:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. processes and activities that may be affected.
texts.text: processes and activities that may be affected.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. how senior management would prefer to respond.
texts.text: how senior management would prefer to respond.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. whether the enterprise qualifies for an exemption.
texts.text: whether the enterprise qualifies for an exemption.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. the approximate cost of compliance.
texts.text: the approximate cost of compliance.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Changes to information security are best made on the basis of risk. To determine the risk associated with the new regulations, the information security manager must first know what processes and activities may be affected.
texts.text: Changes to information security are best made on the basis of risk. To determine the risk associated with the new regulations, the information security manager must first know what processes and activities may be affected.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Senior management will not have a basis for preference until potential effects are determined and compliance requirements are identified.
texts.text: Senior management will not have a basis for preference until potential effects are determined and compliance requirements are identified.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Requesting exemptions comes at a cost, at least in terms of time and potentially with reputational consequences. Also, if there is little or no effect on the enterprise, there will be no need to request an exemption even if one is available.
texts.text: Requesting exemptions comes at a cost, at least in terms of time and potentially with reputational consequences. Also, if there is little or no effect on the enterprise, there will be no need to request an exemption even if one is available.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Until the scope of potential effects and the changes that may be needed to comply are understood, the cost of compliance cannot be reasonably approximated.
texts.text: Until the scope of potential effects and the changes that may be needed to comply are understood, the cost of compliance cannot be reasonably approximated.

texts.orig: 1. An effective risk management program should reduce risk to:
texts.text: An effective risk management program should reduce risk to:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. zero.
texts.text: zero.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. an acceptable level.
texts.text: an acceptable level.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. an acceptable percent of revenue.
texts.text: an acceptable percent of revenue.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. an acceptable probability of occurrence.
texts.text: an acceptable probability of occurrence.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Reducing risk to zero is impossible, and the attempt would be cost-prohibitive.
texts.text: Reducing risk to zero is impossible, and the attempt would be cost-prohibitive.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Tying risk to a percentage of revenue is inadvisable because there is no direct correlation between the two.
texts.text: Tying risk to a percentage of revenue is inadvisable because there is no direct correlation between the two.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. An effective risk management program reduces the risk to an acceptable level; this is achieved by reducing the probability of a loss event through preventive measures and by reducing the impact of a loss event through corrective measures.
texts.text: An effective risk management program reduces the risk to an acceptable level; this is achieved by reducing the probability of a loss event through preventive measures and by reducing the impact of a loss event through corrective measures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Reducing the probability of risk occurrence may not always be possible, as in the case of natural disasters.
texts.text: Reducing the probability of risk occurrence may not always be possible, as in the case of natural disasters.

texts.orig: 2. Which of the following BEST indicates a successful risk management practice?

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Overall risk is quantified.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Inherent risk is eliminated.
texts.text: Inherent risk is eliminated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Residual risk is acceptable.
texts.text: Residual risk is acceptable.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Control risk is tied to business units.
texts.text: Control risk is tied to business units.

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The fact that overall risk has been quantified does not necessarily indicate the existence of a successful risk management practice.
texts.text: The fact that overall risk has been quantified does not necessarily indicate the existence of a successful risk management practice.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Eliminating inherent risk is virtually impossible.
texts.text: Eliminating inherent risk is virtually impossible.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A successful risk management practice reduces residual risk to acceptable levels.
texts.text: A successful risk management practice reduces residual risk to acceptable levels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Although the tying of control risk to business may improve accountability, it is not as desirable as achieving acceptable residual risk levels.
texts.text: Although the tying of control risk to business may improve accountability, it is not as desirable as achieving acceptable residual risk levels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 26. Which of the following is MOST essential when assessing risk?
texts.text: Which of the following is MOST essential when assessing risk?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Providing equal coverage for all asset types
texts.text: Providing equal coverage for all asset types

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Benchmarking data from similar enterprises
texts.text: Benchmarking data from similar enterprises

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Considering both monetary value and likelihoodof loss
texts.text: Considering both monetary value and likelihoodof loss

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Focusing on valid past threats and business losses
texts.text: Focusing on valid past threats and business losses

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Providing equal coverage for all asset types when assessing risk may not be relevant, depending on the significance the asset type has to the enterprise (e.g., the automobile fleet is not likely to have as much significance as the data center).
texts.text: Providing equal coverage for all asset types when assessing risk may not be relevant, depending on the significance the asset type has to the enterprise (e.g., the automobile fleet is not likely to have as much significance as the data center).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Benchmarking other enterprises when assessing risk is of relatively little value.
texts.text: Benchmarking other enterprises when assessing risk is of relatively little value.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The likelihood of loss and the monetary value of those losses are the most essential elements to consider in assessing risk.
texts.text: The likelihood of loss and the monetary value of those losses are the most essential elements to consider in assessing risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Past threats and losses may be instruictive of potential future events but are not the most essential considerations when assessing risk.
texts.text: Past threats and losses may be instruictive of potential future events but are not the most essential considerations when assessing risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. exploitation of a vulnerability in the information system.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: threat actors targeting the enterprise in greater numbers.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: failure of a previously deployed detective control.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. approval of a new exception for noncompliance by management.
texts.text: approval of a new exception for noncompliance by management.

texts.text: Exploitation of a vulnerability is likely to generate an increase in the number of security events.

texts.orig: D. Exceptions approved by management may result in a higher number of security events on reports if notice of the exceptions is not provided to information security to allow updates to monitoring. However, exceptions are typically communicated to the information security manager, so this is an unlikely explanation for the increase.
texts.text: Exceptions approved by management may result in a higher number of security events on reports if notice of the exceptions is not provided to information security to allow updates to monitoring. texts.orig: 51. Which of the following would BEST address the risk of data leakage?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. File backup procedures
texts.text: File backup procedures

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Database integrity checks
texts.text: Database integrity checks

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Acceptable use policies
texts.text: Acceptable use policies

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Incident response procedures
texts.text: Incident response procedures

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. File backup procedures ensure the availability of information in alignment with data retention requirements but do nothing to prevent leakage.
texts.text: File backup procedures ensure the availability of information in alignment with data retention requirements but do nothing to prevent leakage.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Database integrity checks verify the allocation and structural integrity of all the objects in the specified database but do nothing to prevent leakage.
texts.text: Database integrity checks verify the allocation and structural integrity of all the objects in the specified database but do nothing to prevent leakage.

texts.text: An acceptable use policy establishes an agreement between users and the enterprise and defines for all parties the ranges of use that are approved before gaining access to a network or the Internet.

texts.text: Incident response procedures provide detailed steps that help an enterprise minimize the impact of an adverse event but do not directly address data leakage.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 52. Which of the following internal or external influences on an enterprise is the MOST difficult to estimate?
texts.text: Which of the following internal or external influences on an enterprise is the MOST difficult to estimate?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Vulnerability posture
texts.text: Vulnerability posture

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Compliance requirements
texts.text: Compliance requirements

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Outsourcing expenses
texts.text: Outsourcing expenses

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Threat landscape

texts.orig: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The vulnerability posture of an enterprise can be estimated with a high degree of accuracy through systematic, iterative review of systems, data flows, people and processes.
texts.text: The vulnerability posture of an enterprise can be estimated with a high degree of accuracy through systematic, iterative review of systems, data flows, people and processes.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Compliance requirements may be ambiguous at first, but as requirements are reviewed and narrowed, their influence on an enterprise becomes more predictable until the requirements change or expand over time.
texts.text: Compliance requirements may be ambiguous at first, but as requirements are reviewed and narrowed, their influence on an enterprise becomes more predictable until the requirements change or expand over time.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The long-term costs of outsourcing are difficult to predict, but the cost is generally clear for defined periods of time (e.g., contract periods). In contrast, the threat landscape is always difficult to estimate.
texts.text: The long-term costs of outsourcing are difficult to predict, but the cost is generally clear for defined periods of time (e.g., contract periods). In contrast, the threat landscape is always difficult to estimate.

texts.orig: D. Threats originate from independent sources that may be natural or human-directed. Neither can be positively predicted in all cases. Human-directed threats in particular are extremely difficult to estimate in an information security context because very small numbers of threat actors (including individuals with no assistance) may be ready and able to initiate threat events for any reason at all, including reasons that are not sensible to the individual or an impartial observer.

texts.text: Audit the third-party provider to evaluate their security controls.

texts.orig: 58. What is the root cause of a successful cross-site request forgery attack?
texts.text: What is the root cause of a successful cross-site request forgery attack?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The application uses multiple redirects for completing a data commit transaction.
texts.text: The application uses multiple redirects for completing a data commit transaction.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The application has been installed with a non-legitimate license key.
texts.text: The application has been installed with a non-legitimate license key.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The application has implemented cookies as the sole authentication mechanism.
texts.text: The application has implemented cookies as the sole authentication mechanism.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The application is hosted on a server along with other applications.
texts.text: The application is hosted on a server along with other applications.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Cross-site request forgery (XSRF) is related to an authentication mechanism, not to redirection.
texts.text: Cross-site request forgery (XSRF) is related to an authentication mechanism, not to redirection.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. XSRF exploits inadequate authentication mechanisms in web applications that rely only on elements such as cookies when performing a transaction. It is a type of website attack in which unauthorized commands are transmitted from a trusted user.
texts.text: XSRF exploits inadequate authentication mechanisms in web applications that rely only on elements such as cookies when performing a transaction. It is a type of website attack in which unauthorized commands are transmitted from a trusted user.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A non-legitimate license key is related to intellectual property rights, not to XSRF vulnerability.
texts.text: A non-legitimate license key is related to intellectual property rights, not to XSRF vulnerability.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Merely hosting multiple applications on the same server is not the root cause of this vulnerability.
texts.text: Merely hosting multiple applications on the same server is not the root cause of this vulnerability.
