texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 183. Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective approach to test the security of a legacy application?
texts.text: Which of the following is the MOST cost-effective approach to test the security of a legacy application?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Identify a similar application and refer to its security weaknesses.
texts.text: Identify a similar application and refer to its security weaknesses.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Recompile the application using the latest library and review the error codes.
texts.text: Recompile the application using the latest library and review the error codes.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Employ reverse engineering techniques to derive functionalities.
texts.text: Employ reverse engineering techniques to derive functionalities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Conduct a vulnerability assessment to detect application weaknesses.
texts.text: Conduct a vulnerability assessment to detect application weaknesses.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Many applications that appear to be functionally similar may be remarkably dissimilar at the code implementation level. Even a newer version of the same software may have been entirely rewritten, and any software developed in-house is necessarily unique to the environment.
texts.text: Many applications that appear to be functionally similar may be remarkably dissimilar at the code implementation level. Even a newer version of the same software may have been entirely rewritten, and any software developed in-house is necessarily unique to the environment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Recompiling a legacy application is possible only when source code is available. It may not function properly if underlying libraries or coding standards have changed.
texts.text: Recompiling a legacy application is possible only when source code is available. It may not function properly if underlying libraries or coding standards have changed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Reverse engineering a legacy application is likely to cost significantly more than a vulnerability assessment and deriving the functionalities of the application is not the goal.
texts.text: Reverse engineering a legacy application is likely to cost significantly more than a vulnerability assessment and deriving the functionalities of the application is not the goal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Identifying vulnerabilities will allow an enterprise to determine what compensating controls may be needed to continue operating a legacy application where replacement is not an option. Vulnerability assessments are not necessarily comprehensive in all cases, but they are generally effective when planned properly.
texts.text: Identifying vulnerabilities will allow an enterprise to determine what compensating controls may be needed to continue operating a legacy application where replacement is not an option. Vulnerability assessments are not necessarily comprehensive in all cases, but they are generally effective when planned properly.

texts.orig: B. a risk assessment and analysis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 185. Addressing risk scenarios at various inforination system life cycle stages is PRIMARILY a function of:
texts.text: Addressing risk scenarios at various inforination system life cycle stages is PRIMARILY a function of:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. change management.
texts.text: change management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. release management.
texts.text: release management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. incident management.
texts.text: incident management.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Change management is the overall process to assess and control risk scenarios introduced by changes.

texts.text: Release management is the process to manage risk scenarios of production system deployment, and it is a component of change management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Incident management addresses impacts when or after they occur.

texts.text: Configuration management is the specific process to manage risk scenarios associated with systems configuration, and it is a component of change management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 186. Which of the following is the FIRST action to be taken when the information security manager notes that the controls for a critical application are inadequate?
texts.text: Which of the following is the FIRST action to be taken when the information security manager notes that the controls for a critical application are inadequate?

texts.text: Perform a risk assessment to determine the level of exposure.

texts.text: Classify the risk as acceptable to senior management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Deploy additional countermeasures immediately.
texts.text: Deploy additional countermeasures immediately.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Transfer the remaining risk to another enterprise.
texts.text: Transfer the remaining risk to another enterprise.

texts.orig: B. The exposure level needs to be redetermined and compared with the residual risk before this decision can be made.
texts.text: The exposure level needs to be redetermined and compared with the residual risk before this decision can be made.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Risk transfer is an action that may be taken after reviewing the results of the risk assessment of the current situation.
texts.text: Risk transfer is an action that may be taken after reviewing the results of the risk assessment of the current situation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Additional countermeasures may be deployed after determining possible losses to avoid overprotecting or underprotecting the asset.

texts.orig: 187. Which of the following is the GREATEST concern for an enterprise in which there is a widespread use of mobile devices?
texts.text: Which of the following is the GREATEST concern for an enterprise in which there is a widespread use of mobile devices?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. There is an undue reliance on public networks.
texts.text: There is an undue reliance on public networks.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Batteries require constant recharges.
texts.text: Batteries require constant recharges.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. There is a lack of operating system standardization.
texts.text: There is a lack of operating system standardization.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Mobile devices can be easily lost or stolen.
texts.text: Mobile devices can be easily lost or stolen.

texts.label: section_header

texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The fact that mobile devices must be connected to public networks creates a security risk that can be exploited in the public space, but appropriate security controls can mitigate the risk.
texts.text: The fact that mobile devices must be connected to public networks creates a security risk that can be exploited in the public space, but appropriate security controls can mitigate the risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The need to constantly recharge batteries is not a significant security concern.
texts.text: The need to constantly recharge batteries is not a significant security concern.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. While the lack of operating system standardization is a concern, it is not as great as the loss of devices.

texts.orig: 188. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate to communicate to senior management to enable them to make ongoing, timely decisions on current information security risk?

texts.label: list_item

Reporting KRIs to senior management would help them make decisions on current risk, such as adjusting or replacing the controls that are mitigating them. KRIs continuously alert senior management to make management risk decisions.

texts.orig: C. Internal and external loss data show past information risk but not current risk.

texts.orig: 196. Which of the following authentication methods is MOST the secure when users require remote access to production systems?
texts.text: Which of the following authentication methods is MOST the secure when users require remote access to production systems?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A one-time password
texts.text: A one-time password

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A virtual private network
texts.text: A virtual private network

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Multifactor authentication
texts.text: Multifactor authentication

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Complex passwords
texts.text: Complex passwords

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. One-time passwords are more secure than static passwords, but alone, they are not the most secure method.
texts.text: One-time passwords are more secure than static passwords, but alone, they are not the most secure method.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A virtual private network is an encryption connection from a device to a network; it is not an authentication method.
texts.text: A virtual private network is an encryption connection from a device to a network; it is not an authentication method.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Multifactor authentication is the most secure way to authenticate users when remote access to production system is required. Multifactor authentication uses three common factors: something you know (e.g., passwords), something you have (e.g., tokens, smart cards) and something you are (e.g., biometric methods such as fingerprints or retina scans). A complex password includes two out of three common factors used for multifactor authentication.
texts.text: Multifactor authentication is the most secure way to authenticate users when remote access to production system is required. Multifactor authentication uses three common factors: something you know (e.g., passwords), something you have (e.g., tokens, smart cards) and something you are (e.g., biometric methods such as fingerprints or retina scans). A complex password includes two out of three common factors used for multifactor authentication.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Requiring complex passwords is a good practice, but it is not the most secure method.
texts.text: Requiring complex passwords is a good practice, but it is not the most secure method.

texts.orig: 201. Which of the following will be the MOST likely exploitation target when looking at flaws in application controls?
texts.text: Which of the following will be the MOST likely exploitation target when looking at flaws in application controls?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Password change options at the login stage
texts.text: Password change options at the login stage

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Weak transaction monitoring controls
texts.text: Weak transaction monitoring controls

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Inadequate validation checks in entry forms
texts.text: Inadequate validation checks in entry forms

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Open ports available for external access
texts.text: Open ports available for external access

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Password cracking by exploiting a password change option may not be easy unless the perpetrator obtains a valid password in advance. Hence, attackers prefer to look for weaknesses in validation checks in the application control layer.
texts.text: Password cracking by exploiting a password change option may not be easy unless the perpetrator obtains a valid password in advance. Hence, attackers prefer to look for weaknesses in validation checks in the application control layer.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Weak or nonexistent transaction monitoring controls can be a target for exploitation; however, controls with nonexistent or inadequate validation checks are an easier target for attackers.
texts.text: Weak or nonexistent transaction monitoring controls can be a target for exploitation; however, controls with nonexistent or inadequate validation checks are an easier target for attackers.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Many attackers exploit weaknesses existing in the application layer. A weak validation check-in entry screen may be vulnerable to structured query language (SQL) injection attacks. Hence, validation control is a key feature in application controls.
texts.text: Many attackers exploit weaknesses existing in the application layer. A weak validation check-in entry screen may be vulnerable to structured query language (SQL) injection attacks. Hence, validation control is a key feature in application controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Control of open ports may be handled by network administration, which is separate from the application control layer. Hence, it is unlikely that attackers exploiting application weaknesses will look for open ports.
texts.text: Control of open ports may be handled by network administration, which is separate from the application control layer. Hence, it is unlikely that attackers exploiting application weaknesses will look for open ports.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 202. Which of the following will be the MAJOR concern when an employee connects an unauthorized personal device to the enterprise's network?
texts.text: Which of the following will be the MAJOR concern when an employee connects an unauthorized personal device to the enterprise's network?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Unintended release of malware
texts.text: Unintended release of malware

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Inadvertent loss of the personal device
texts.text: Inadvertent loss of the personal device

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Undetected messaging among staff
texts.text: Undetected messaging among staff

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Slowdown of network performance
texts.text: Slowdown of network performance

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. An uncontrolled technical device owned by an employee usually contains fewer controls and protective security measures than an enterprise device and, therefore, might be infected with malware. Connecting this type of device to the enterprise's network is a major risk as malware will infiltrate the enterprise, bypassing firewalls. Employees need to be educated on the proper use of personal technical devices, and an acceptable use or Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policy should be in place.
texts.text: An uncontrolled technical device owned by an employee usually contains fewer controls and protective security measures than an enterprise device and, therefore, might be infected with malware. Connecting this type of device to the enterprise's network is a major risk as malware will infiltrate the enterprise, bypassing firewalls. Employees need to be educated on the proper use of personal technical devices, and an acceptable use or Bring Your Own Device (BYOD) policy should be in place.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The loss of the device would present an issue; however, this would be secondary to a potential malware infection.
texts.text: The loss of the device would present an issue; however, this would be secondary to a potential malware infection.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Messaging among staff using personal devices would not be as big of a concern as the release of malware into the network.
texts.text: Messaging among staff using personal devices would not be as big of a concern as the release of malware into the network.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. It is unlikely that network performance slows down as the result of personal devices connecting to the enterprise network.
texts.text: It is unlikely that network performance slows down as the result of personal devices connecting to the enterprise network.

texts.orig: 203. An enterprise security risk assessment was conducted based on assumptions about enterprise risk. Which of the following would be the BEST course of action to improve the quality of the assessment?
texts.text: An enterprise security risk assessment was conducted based on assumptions about enterprise risk. Which of the following would be the BEST course of action to improve the quality of the assessment?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Recruit experienced interviewers to the assessment team
texts.text: Recruit experienced interviewers to the assessment team

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Review past risk assessments for background information
texts.text: Review past risk assessments for background information

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Request that business units classify information assets
texts.text: Request that business units classify information assets

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Include relevant stakeholders during assessment activities
texts.text: Include relevant stakeholders during assessment activities

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Skilled interviewers may help in conducting risk assessments; however, interview skills alone may not resolve this typeof problem.
texts.text: Skilled interviewers may help in conducting risk assessments; however, interview skills alone may not resolve this typeof problem.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Past risk assessments may not be relevant to the current state of the enterprise.
texts.text: Past risk assessments may not be relevant to the current state of the enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Classification of information assets is a part of an information security program conducted in the business area. It does not affect how an information security risk assessment is currently conducted.
texts.text: Classification of information assets is a part of an information security program conducted in the business area. It does not affect how an information security risk assessment is currently conducted.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Including relevant stakeholders is an ideal way to move beyond a risk assessment based on assumptions, as they can provide essential insight that would otherwise be missed.
texts.text: Including relevant stakeholders is an ideal way to move beyond a risk assessment based on assumptions, as they can provide essential insight that would otherwise be missed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 204. The human resources (HR) department is planning to introduce a procedure to deactivate an employee record within 24 hours of termination of employment. Which of the following would be of MOST concern to: the information security manager when reviewing this procedure?
texts.text: The human resources (HR) department is planning to introduce a procedure to deactivate an employee record within 24 hours of termination of employment. Which of the following would be of MOST concern to: the information security manager when reviewing this procedure?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Potential internal fraud to circumvent the controls in place
texts.text: Potential internal fraud to circumvent the controls in place

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Interdependencies between HR systems and business systems
texts.text: Interdependencies between HR systems and business systems

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Integrity of the HR system record to produce a job assignment history
texts.text: Integrity of the HR system record to produce a job assignment history

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Justification of 24 hours from risk management perspective
texts.text: Justification of 24 hours from risk management perspective

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. There is a possibility of internal fraud by: a terminated employee, but this is a less severe threat than the interdependencies. between HR systems and other business operations.
texts.text: There is a possibility of internal fraud by: a terminated employee, but this is a less severe threat than the interdependencies. between HR systems and other business operations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Production systems will refer to the human resources (HR) database to check the identity of employees. If the reference to an employee attribute is lost during business transactions, it may affect business processes. (For instance, the financial ledger system may reject journal entries rela  es s s e  a d se re-o  etsy etc.) Thus, dependencies within the production systems need to be reviewed before this procedure is implemented.
texts.text: Production systems will refer to the human resources (HR) database to check the identity of employees. If the reference to an employee attribute is lost during business transactions, it may affect business processes. (For instance, the financial ledger system may reject journal entries rela  es s s e  a d se re-o  etsy etc.) Thus, dependencies within the production systems need to be reviewed before this procedure is implemented.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. It is not common to generate a job assignment history of employees after termination. Therefore, the integrity of a record is not a priority.
texts.text: It is not common to generate a job assignment history of employees after termination. Therefore, the integrity of a record is not a priority.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Justification of timeframe (e.g., 24 hours) in a procedure may be evaluated by business and security management and then mutually signed off on. Unless there are any specific issues, this will not be a major concern.
texts.text: Justification of timeframe (e.g., 24 hours) in a procedure may be evaluated by business and security management and then mutually signed off on. Unless there are any specific issues, this will not be a major concern.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 205. One of the MOST important internal critical factors that affects the information security strategy is:
texts.text: One of the MOST important internal critical factors that affects the information security strategy is:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. a well-defined organizational structure.
texts.text: a well-defined organizational structure.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. widespread promoted IT security awareness.
texts.text: widespread promoted IT security awareness.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. the organizational security culture.
texts.text: the organizational security culture.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. established enterprise risk appetite and tolerance levels.
texts.text: established enterprise risk appetite and tolerance levels.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A well-defined organizational structure could be an enabler for an effective security strategy, but it is not the most important factor.
texts.text: A well-defined organizational structure could be an enabler for an effective security strategy, but it is not the most important factor.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A lack of internal IT security awareness could be part of the threat landscape, but it is not as important as the risk appetite and tolerance.
texts.text: A lack of internal IT security awareness could be part of the threat landscape, but it is not as important as the risk appetite and tolerance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Enterprise security culture may have an impact on the information security strategy; however, enterprise risk appetite still has the biggest impact.
texts.text: Enterprise security culture may have an impact on the information security strategy; however, enterprise risk appetite still has the biggest impact.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The security strategy is primarily led by an established enterprise risk appetite and levels.
texts.text: The security strategy is primarily led by an established enterprise risk appetite and levels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 206. What is the PRIMARY reason an enterprise would study cybersecurity threats? To establish:
texts.text: What is the PRIMARY reason an enterprise would study cybersecurity threats? To establish:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. a threat library.
texts.text: a threat library.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. a control baseline.
texts.text: a control baseline.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. incident response playbooks.
texts.text: incident response playbooks.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. a threat analysis.
texts.text: a threat analysis.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Threat libraries may be compiled in the course of threat analysis, but updating the threat library is not the main reason to study cybersecurity threats.
texts.text: Threat libraries may be compiled in the course of threat analysis, but updating the threat library is not the main reason to study cybersecurity threats.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Although studying cybersecurity threats may help in designing and baselining controls, creating a control baseline is based on the overall risk (business impact), not threats alone.
texts.text: Although studying cybersecurity threats may help in designing and baselining controls, creating a control baseline is based on the overall risk (business impact), not threats alone.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. An incident response playbook is set of processes for responding and resolving incidents. Studying cyberthreats certainly adds to an incident response plan, but that is not the reason to conduct cybersecurity threat analysis.
texts.text: An incident response playbook is set of processes for responding and resolving incidents. Studying cyberthreats certainly adds to an incident response plan, but that is not the reason to conduct cybersecurity threat analysis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The main goal of threat analysis is to understand how the enterprise is positioned in the threat landscape. Threat analysis also supports decisions to prioritize control activities to mitigate the most critical risk. Threat analysis is an important factor in calculating risk value.
texts.text: The main goal of threat analysis is to understand how the enterprise is positioned in the threat landscape. Threat analysis also supports decisions to prioritize control activities to mitigate the most critical risk. Threat analysis is an important factor in calculating risk value.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 207. Which of the following processes is PRIMARILY supported by information asset identification and classification?
texts.text: Which of the following processes is PRIMARILY supported by information asset identification and classification?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Risk register development
texts.text: Risk register development

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Risk assessment
texts.text: Risk assessment

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Cybersecurity training program
texts.text: Cybersecurity training program

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Regulatory compliance requirement
texts.text: Regulatory compliance requirement

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Tracking risk in a register is important, but it is not solely based on the classification of the asset.
texts.text: Tracking risk in a register is important, but it is not solely based on the classification of the asset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Unless assets are identified and classified, it will not be possible to assess the risk associated with each asset.
texts.text: Unless assets are identified and classified, it will not be possible to assess the risk associated with each asset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Cybersecurity training should be risk-based. However, user training is typically based on a scenario, such as phishing.
texts.text: Cybersecurity training should be risk-based. However, user training is typically based on a scenario, such as phishing.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D: While addressing compliance risk is valid, the key benefit goes beyond compliance because classification assists the enterprise in protecting the assets through incident response. If the incident response plan is lacking, the enterprise would consider additional policy statements to protect higher priority assets. Incident response plans are often safety nets for limiting damage when a control fails or does not exist.
texts.text: D: While addressing compliance risk is valid, the key benefit goes beyond compliance because classification assists the enterprise in protecting the assets through incident response. If the incident response plan is lacking, the enterprise would consider additional policy statements to protect higher priority assets. Incident response plans are often safety nets for limiting damage when a control fails or does not exist.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 208. Which of the following should be completed prior to a risk assessment?
texts.text: Which of the following should be completed prior to a risk assessment?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Control identification
texts.text: Control identification

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Asset identification
texts.text: Asset identification

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Threat identification
texts.text: Threat identification

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Risk register identification
texts.text: Risk register identification

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Controls are evaluated after assets are identified as part of the risk assessment process.
texts.text: Controls are evaluated after assets are identified as part of the risk assessment process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Asset identification must be completed prior to risk assessment because it is the basis of the risk assessment.
texts.text: Asset identification must be completed prior to risk assessment because it is the basis of the risk assessment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Threats are identified after assets are identified as part of the risk assessment process.
texts.text: Threats are identified after assets are identified as part of the risk assessment process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The risk register is a catalog of risk categories or an inventory of risks identified and is not part of the risk assessment process.
texts.text: The risk register is a catalog of risk categories or an inventory of risks identified and is not part of the risk assessment process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 209. Inherent cybersecurity risk is treated via:
texts.text: Inherent cybersecurity risk is treated via:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Internet firewalls.
texts.text: Internet firewalls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. security awareness.
texts.text: security awareness.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. risk assessment.
texts.text: risk assessment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. controls.
texts.text: controls.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Internet firewalls are only one kind of control and do not constitute a comprehensive approach to reducing risk in cybersecurity.
texts.text: Internet firewalls are only one kind of control and do not constitute a comprehensive approach to reducing risk in cybersecurity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. In the absence of controls that mitigate risk, cybersecurity risk will remain the same regardless of awareness efforts.
texts.text: In the absence of controls that mitigate risk, cybersecurity risk will remain the same regardless of awareness efforts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Risk assessments may be used to guide risk response, but on their own, they do not treat inherent risk.
texts.text: Risk assessments may be used to guide risk response, but on their own, they do not treat inherent risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. A risk prior to mitigation is called inherent risk. The risk that remains after countermeasures and controls have been implemented is residual risk. Controls are most often used to treat the risk after the risk is analyzed.
texts.text: A risk prior to mitigation is called inherent risk. The risk that remains after countermeasures and controls have been implemented is residual risk. Controls are most often used to treat the risk after the risk is analyzed.

texts.orig: 210. A solution using an emerging security technology may allow an enterprise to increase its revenue, but the technology remains unproven. Which of the following is the BEST approach to take when considering use of the technology?
texts.text: A solution using an emerging security technology may allow an enterprise to increase its revenue, but the technology remains unproven. Which of the following is the BEST approach to take when considering use of the technology?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Hold until competitors introduce the solution.
texts.text: Hold until competitors introduce the solution.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Run a pilot project to assess potential risk.
texts.text: Run a pilot project to assess potential risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Build the solution in a vendor's environment.
texts.text: Build the solution in a vendor's environment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Obtain insurance to cover unexpected losses.
texts.text: Obtain insurance to cover unexpected losses.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Bis the correct answer.
texts.text: Bis the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Management may advise holding off until a competitor implements the technology; however, the enterprise would then lose out on any potential revenue presented by the opportunity. This decision is best made once potential risk is assessed.
texts.text: Management may advise holding off until a competitor implements the technology; however, the enterprise would then lose out on any potential revenue presented by the opportunity. This decision is best made once potential risk is assessed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. When considering using unproven, emerging technologies, it is best to start small. A pilot project will be best suited for this purpose because risk can be assessed in a controlled manner as the business explores the viability of the technology and potential further deployment on a larger scale.
texts.text: When considering using unproven, emerging technologies, it is best to start small. A pilot project will be best suited for this purpose because risk can be assessed in a controlled manner as the business explores the viability of the technology and potential further deployment on a larger scale.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Even when the solution is built in a service vendor's technical environment, the service requestor must own the risk stemming from the technical solution. Therefore, the enterprise will want to assess the potential risk first.
texts.text: Even when the solution is built in a service vendor's technical environment, the service requestor must own the risk stemming from the technical solution. Therefore, the enterprise will want to assess the potential risk first.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. It is not common practice to buy insurance in anticipation of failures may be caused by unproven technology.
texts.text: It is not common practice to buy insurance in anticipation of failures may be caused by unproven technology.

texts.orig: A. Threat analysis
texts.text: Threat analysis

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Impact assessment
texts.text: Impact assessment

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Controls evaluation
texts.text: Controls evaluation

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header

texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Threat analysis only identifies the threats that exist against enterprise assets. However, threat and impact need to be taken into account.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Controls evaluation is needed after classification levels have been determined to ensure that the asset is protected according to the classification level.

texts.orig: The classification level is an indication of the value or importance of the asset to the enterprise. Impact assessments are needed to determine criticality and sensitivity, which form the basis for the classification level.
texts.text: The classification level is an indication of the value or importance of the asset to the enterprise. Impact assessments are needed to determine criticality and sensitivity, which form the basis for the classification level.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Penetration testing is not one of the prerequisites for conducting asset classification.
texts.text: Penetration testing is not one of the prerequisites for conducting asset classification.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Decentralized access control is not a type of access control but an administrative approach.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Discretionary access control would require a greater degree of administrative overhead because it is based on each individual rather than on groups of individuals.
texts.text: Discretionary access control would require a greater degree of administrative overhead because it is based on each individual rather than on groups of individuals.

texts.orig: 6. When designing an intrusion detection system, the information security manager should recommend that it be placed:
texts.text: When designing an intrusion detection system, the information security manager should recommend that it be placed:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. outside the firewall.
texts.text: outside the firewall.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. on the firewall server.
texts.text: on the firewall server.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. on a screened subnet.
texts.text: on a screened subnet.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. on the external router.
texts.text: on the external router.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Placing the intrusion detection system (IDS) on the Internet side of the firewall is not advised because the system will generate alerts on all malicious traffic—even though 99 percent will be stopped by the firewall and never reach the internal network.
texts.text: Placing the intrusion detection system (IDS) on the Internet side of the firewall is not advised because the system will generate alerts on all malicious traffic—even though 99 percent will be stopped by the firewall and never reach the internal network.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Because firewalls should be installed on hardened servers with minimal services enabled, it would be inappropriate to install the IDS on the same physical device.
texts.text: Because firewalls should be installed on hardened servers with minimal services enabled, it would be inappropriate to install the IDS on the same physical device.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. An IDS should be placed on a screened subnet, which is a demilitarized zone.
texts.text: An IDS should be placed on a screened subnet, which is a demilitarized zone.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Placing the IDS on the external server, even if it were feasible, is not advised because the system will generate alerts on all malicious traffic—even though 99 percent will be stopped by the firewall and never reach the internal network.
texts.text: Placing the IDS on the external server, even if it were feasible, is not advised because the system will generate alerts on all malicious traffic—even though 99 percent will be stopped by the firewall and never reach the internal network.

texts.orig: 7. The BEST reason for an enterprise to implement two discrete firewalls connected directly to the Internet and the same demilitarized zone would be to:
texts.text: The BEST reason for an enterprise to implement two discrete firewalls connected directly to the Internet and the same demilitarized zone would be to:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. provide in-depth defense.
texts.text: provide in-depth defense.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. separate test and production.
texts.text: separate test and production.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. permit traffic load balancing.
texts.text: permit traffic load balancing.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. prevent a denial-of-service attack.
texts.text: prevent a denial-of-service attack.

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Two firewalls in parallel provide two concurrent paths for compromise and, therefore, do not provide defense in depth. If they were connected in a series, one behind the other, they would provide defense in depth.
texts.text: Two firewalls in parallel provide two concurrent paths for compromise and, therefore, do not provide defense in depth. If they were connected in a series, one behind the other, they would provide defense in depth.

texts.orig: B. As both entry points connect tó the Internet and to the same demilitarized zone, such an arrangement is not practical for separating testing from production.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Having two entry points, each guarded by a separate firewall, is desirable to permit traffic load balancing.
texts.text: Having two entry points, each guarded by a separate firewall, is desirable to permit traffic load balancing.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Firewalls are not effective at preventing denial-of-service attacks.
texts.text: Firewalls are not effective at preventing denial-of-service attacks.

texts.orig: 10. Which of the following factors BEST helps determine the appropriate protection level for an information asset?
texts.text: Which of the following factors BEST helps determine the appropriate protection level for an information asset?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The cost of acquisition and implementation of the asset
texts.text: The cost of acquisition and implementation of the asset

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Knowledge of vulnerabilities present in the asset
texts.text: Knowledge of vulnerabilities present in the asset

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The degree of exposure to known threats
texts.text: The degree of exposure to known threats

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The criticality of the business function supported by the asset
texts.text: The criticality of the business function supported by the asset

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The criticality of the asset is determined by the business value of the asset, not just the cost of the asset. The value is determined by the cost of acquisition and implementation of the asset.
texts.text: The criticality of the asset is determined by the business value of the asset, not just the cost of the asset. The value is determined by the cost of acquisition and implementation of the asset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Knowledge of vulnerabilities helps in determining the protection method; however, protection is implemented based on the business value of the asset compared with the cost of the protection method.
texts.text: Knowledge of vulnerabilities helps in determining the protection method; however, protection is implemented based on the business value of the asset compared with the cost of the protection method.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The degree of exposure may require certain treatment options, but the degree and extent of protection is still determined by criticality.
texts.text: The degree of exposure may require certain treatment options, but the degree and extent of protection is still determined by criticality.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Although all the options may help in determining the protection level of the asset, the criticality of the business function supported by the asset is the most important because nonavailability might affect the delivery of services.

texts.orig: 11. Which of the following is the BEST metric for evaluating the effectiveness of an intrusion detection mechanism?
texts.text: Which of the following is the BEST metric for evaluating the effectiveness of an intrusion detection mechanism?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Number of attacks detected
texts.text: Number of attacks detected

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Number of successful attacks
texts.text: Number of successful attacks

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Ratio of false positives to false negatives
texts.text: Ratio of false positives to false negatives

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Ratio of successful to unsuccessful attacks
texts.text: Ratio of successful to unsuccessful attacks

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The number of attacks detected does not indicate how many attacks were not detected; therefore, it is no indication of effectiveness.
texts.text: The number of attacks detected does not indicate how many attacks were not detected; therefore, it is no indication of effectiveness.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The number of successful attacks cannot be used as a metric to evaluate the effectiveness of an intrusion detection mechanism.
texts.text: The number of successful attacks cannot be used as a metric to evaluate the effectiveness of an intrusion detection mechanism.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The ratio of false positives to false negatives will indicate the effectiveness of the intrusion detection system.
texts.text: The ratio of false positives to false negatives will indicate the effectiveness of the intrusion detection system.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Without knowing whether attacks were detected or not, the ratio of successful attacks to unsuccessful attacks indicates nothing about the effectiveness of the IDS.
texts.text: Without knowing whether attacks were detected or not, the ratio of successful attacks to unsuccessful attacks indicates nothing about the effectiveness of the IDS.

texts.orig: 12. Which of the following is MOST effective. in preventing weaknesses from being introduced into existing production systems?
texts.text: Which of the following is MOST effective. in preventing weaknesses from being introduced into existing production systems?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Patch management
texts.text: Patch management

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Change management
texts.text: Change management

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Security baselines
texts.text: Security baselines

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Virus detection
texts.text: Virus detection

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Patch management involves the correction of software weaknesses and would necessarily follow change management procedures.
texts.text: Patch management involves the correction of software weaknesses and would necessarily follow change management procedures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Change management controls the process of introducing changes to systems and controlling unauthorized changes to production, which are often the points at which weaknesses will be introduced.
texts.text: Change management controls the process of introducing changes to systems and controlling unauthorized changes to production, which are often the points at which weaknesses will be introduced.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Security baselines provide minimum recommended settings and do not prevent the introduction of control weaknesses.
texts.text: Security baselines provide minimum recommended settings and do not prevent the introduction of control weaknesses.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Virus detection is an effective tool but primarily focuses on malicious code from external sources. It is unrelated to the introduction of vulnerabilities.
texts.text: Virus detection is an effective tool but primarily focuses on malicious code from external sources. It is unrelated to the introduction of vulnerabilities.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Configuration management

texts.text: Justification:

texts.text: Patch management corrects discovered weaknesses by applying a correction (a patch) to the original program code.

texts.orig: 44. From an information security perspective, information that no longer supports the main purpose of the business should be:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. analyzed under the retention policy.
texts.text: analyzed under the retention policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. protected under the information classification policy.
texts.text: protected under the information classification policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. analyzed under the backup policy.
texts.text: analyzed under the backup policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. assessed by a business impact analysis.
texts.text: assessed by a business impact analysis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Information analyzed under the retention policy will determine whether the enterprise is required to maintain the data for business, legal or regulatory reasons. texts.orig: 45. In the process of deploying a new email system, an information security manager would like to ensure the confidentiality of messages while in transit. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate method to ensure data confidentiality in a new email system implementation?
texts.text: In the process of deploying a new email system, an information security manager would like to ensure the confidentiality of messages while in transit. Which of the following is the MOST appropriate method to ensure data confidentiality in a new email system implementation?

texts.orig: A. Properly developed organizational policies are not likely to require any change when corporate standards change due to new technology.
texts.text: Properly developed organizational policies are not likely to require any change when corporate standards change due to new technology.

texts.text: A control objective is a statement of the desired result or purpose to be achieved by implementing control procedures in a particular process. Properly developed control objectives are not likely to-require any changes when corporate standards change due to new technology.

texts.orig: 48. Which of the following practices completely prevents a man-in-the-middle attack between two hosts?
texts.text: Which of the following practices completely prevents a man-in-the-middle attack between two hosts?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Use security tokens for authentication.
texts.text: Use security tokens for authentication.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Connect through an IP Security v6 virtual private network.
texts.text: Connect through an IP Security v6 virtual private network.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Use Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure with a server-side certificate.
texts.text: Use Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure with a server-side certificate.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Enforce static media access control addresses.
texts.text: Enforce static media access control addresses.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Using token-based authentication does not prevent a man-in-the-middle attack; however, it may help eliminate reusability of stolen cleartext credentials.
texts.text: Using token-based authentication does not prevent a man-in-the-middle attack; however, it may help eliminate reusability of stolen cleartext credentials.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. IP Security v6 effectively prevents man-in-the-middle attacks by including source and destination Internet Protocols within the encrypted portion of the packet. The protocol is:resilient to man-inthe-middle attacks.
texts.text: IP Security v6 effectively prevents man-in-the-middle attacks by including source and destination Internet Protocols within the encrypted portion of the packet. The protocol is:resilient to man-inthe-middle attacks.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure session can be intercepted through Domain Name System (DNS) or Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) poisoning.
texts.text: A Hypertext Transfer Protocol Secure session can be intercepted through Domain Name System (DNS) or Address Resolution Protocol (ARP) poisoning.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. ARP poisoning—a specific kind of man-in-the-middle attack—may be prevented by setting static media access control addresses. Nevertheless, DNS and NetBIOS resolution can still be attacked to deviate traffic.
texts.text: ARP poisoning—a specific kind of man-in-the-middle attack—may be prevented by setting static media access control addresses. Nevertheless, DNS and NetBIOS resolution can still be attacked to deviate traffic.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 49. What is the MOST common protocol to ensure confidentiality of transmissions in a business-to-customer financial web application?
texts.text: What is the MOST common protocol to ensure confidentiality of transmissions in a business-to-customer financial web application?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Secure Sockets Layer
texts.text: Secure Sockets Layer

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Secure Shell
texts.text: Secure Shell

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. IP Security
texts.text: IP Security

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions
texts.text: Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Secure Sockets Layer is a cryptographic protocol that provides secure communications, providing end point authentication and communications privacy over the Internet. In typical use, all data transmitted between the customer and the business are, therefore, encrypted by the business's web server and remain confidential.
texts.text: Secure Sockets Layer is a cryptographic protocol that provides secure communications, providing end point authentication and communications privacy over the Internet. In typical use, all data transmitted between the customer and the business are, therefore, encrypted by the business's web server and remain confidential.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Secure Shell (SSH) File Transfer Protocol is a network protocol that provides file transfer and manipulation functionality over any reliable data stream. It is typically used with the SSH-2 protocol to provide secure file transfer.
texts.text: Secure Shell (SSH) File Transfer Protocol is a network protocol that provides file transfer and manipulation functionality over any reliable data stream. It is typically used with the SSH-2 protocol to provide secure file transfer.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. IP Security (IPSec) is a standardized framework for securing Internet Protocol (IP) communications by encrypting and/or authenticating each IP packet in a data stream. There are two modes of IPSec operation: transport mode and tunnel mode.
texts.text: IP Security (IPSec) is a standardized framework for securing Internet Protocol (IP) communications by encrypting and/or authenticating each IP packet in a data stream. There are two modes of IPSec operation: transport mode and tunnel mode.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) is a standard for public key encryption and signing of email encapsulatedin MIME; it is not a web transaction protocol.
texts.text: Secure/Multipurpose Internet Mail Extensions (S/MIME) is a standard for public key encryption and signing of email encapsulatedin MIME; it is not a web transaction protocol.

texts.orig: 54. Which of the following choices is the WEAKEST link in the authorized user registration process?
texts.text: Which of the following choices is the WEAKEST link in the authorized user registration process?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The certificate authority's private key
texts.text: The certificate authority's private key

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The registration authority's private key
texts.text: The registration authority's private key

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The relying party's private key
texts.text: The relying party's private key

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: A secured communication private key

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The certificate authority's (CA's) private key is heavily secured both electronically and physically and is extremely difficult to access by anyone.
texts.text: The certificate authority's (CA's) private key is heavily secured both electronically and physically and is extremely difficult to access by anyone.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The registration authority's (RA's) private key is in the possession of the RA, often stored on a smart card or laptop, and is typically protected by a password and, therefore, is potentially accessible. If the RA's private key is compromised, it can be used to register anyone for a certificate using any identity, compromising the entire public key infrastructure for that CA.
texts.text: The registration authority's (RA's) private key is in the possession of the RA, often stored on a smart card or laptop, and is typically protected by a password and, therefore, is potentially accessible. If the RA's private key is compromised, it can be used to register anyone for a certificate using any identity, compromising the entire public key infrastructure for that CA.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The relying party's private key, if compromised, only puts that party at risk.
texts.text: The relying party's private key, if compromised, only puts that party at risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The private key used for secure communication will only pose a risk to the parties communicating.
texts.text: The private key used for secure communication will only pose a risk to the parties communicating.

texts.orig: 57. Assuming that the value of information assets is known, which of the following gives the information security manager the MOST objective basis for determining that the information security program is delivering value?
texts.text: Assuming that the value of information assets is known, which of the following gives the information security manager the MOST objective basis for determining that the information security program is delivering value?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Number of controls
texts.text: Number of controls

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Cost of achieving control objectives
texts.text: Cost of achieving control objectives

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Effectiveness of controls
texts.text: Effectiveness of controls

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Test results of controls
texts.text: Test results of controls

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Number of controls has no correlation with the value of assets unless the effectiveness of the controls and their cost are also evaluated.
texts.text: Number of controls has no correlation with the value of assets unless the effectiveness of the controls and their cost are also evaluated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A comparison of the cost of achievement of control objectives with the corresponding value of assets sought to be protected would provide a sound basis for the information security manager to measure value delivery.
texts.text: A comparison of the cost of achievement of control objectives with the corresponding value of assets sought to be protected would provide a sound basis for the information security manager to measure value delivery.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Effectiveness of controls has no correlation with the value of assets unless their costs are also evaluated.
texts.text: Effectiveness of controls has no correlation with the value of assets unless their costs are also evaluated.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Test results of controls may determine their effectiveness but has no correlation with the value of assets.
texts.text: Test results of controls may determine their effectiveness but has no correlation with the value of assets.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 58. The use of public key encryption for the purpose of providing encryption keys for a large number of individuals is preferred PRIMARILY because:
texts.text: The use of public key encryption for the purpose of providing encryption keys for a large number of individuals is preferred PRIMARILY because:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. public key encryption is computationally more efficient.
texts.text: public key encryption is computationally more efficient.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. scaling is less problematic than using a symmetrical key.
texts.text: scaling is less problematic than using a symmetrical key.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. public key encryption is less costly to maintain than symmetrical keys for small groups.
texts.text: public key encryption is less costly to maintain than symmetrical keys for small groups.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. public key encryption provides greater encryption strength than secret key options.
texts.text: public key encryption provides greater encryption strength than secret key options.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Public key encryption is computationally intensive due to the long key lengths required.
texts.text: Public key encryption is computationally intensive due to the long key lengths required.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Symmetrical or secret key encryption requires a key for each pair of individuals who wish to have confidential communications resulting in an exponential increase in the number of keys resulting in intractable distribution and storage problems.
texts.text: Symmetrical or secret key encryption requires a key for each pair of individuals who wish to have confidential communications resulting in an exponential increase in the number of keys resulting in intractable distribution and storage problems.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Public key infrastructure is more costly for small groups but less costly to maintain as the participant numbers increase. It is the only manageable option for large groups, which is why it is preferable.
texts.text: Public key infrastructure is more costly for small groups but less costly to maintain as the participant numbers increase. It is the only manageable option for large groups, which is why it is preferable.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Secret key encryption requires much shorter key lengths to achieve equivalent strength.
texts.text: Secret key encryption requires much shorter key lengths to achieve equivalent strength.

texts.orig: 70. What is a desirable sensitivity setting for a biometric access control system that protects a high-security data center?
texts.text: What is a desirable sensitivity setting for a biometric access control system that protects a high-security data center?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A high false reject rate
texts.text: A high false reject rate

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A high false acceptance rate
texts.text: A high false acceptance rate

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Lower than the crossover error rate
texts.text: Lower than the crossover error rate

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The exact crossover error rate
texts.text: The exact crossover error rate

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Biometric access control systems are not infallible. When tuning the solution, one has to adjust the sensitivity level to give preference either to false reject rate (FRR) (type I error rate) making the system more prone to err denying access to a valid user, or to èrr allow access to an invalid user. The preferable setting will be in the FRR region of sensitivity.
texts.text: Biometric access control systems are not infallible. When tuning the solution, one has to adjust the sensitivity level to give preference either to false reject rate (FRR) (type I error rate) making the system more prone to err denying access to a valid user, or to èrr allow access to an invalid user. The preferable setting will be in the FRR region of sensitivity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A high false acceptance rate (FAR) will marginalize security by allowing too much unauthorized access. In systems in which the possibility of false rejects is a problem, it may be necessary to reduce sensitivity and thereby increase the number of false accepts.
texts.text: A high false acceptance rate (FAR) will marginalize security by allowing too much unauthorized access. In systems in which the possibility of false rejects is a problem, it may be necessary to reduce sensitivity and thereby increase the number of false accepts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The crossover rate is sometimes referred to as equal error rate. In a very sensitive system, it may be desirable to minimize the number of false accepts—the number of unauthorized persons allowed access. To do this, the system is tuned to be more sensitive with a lower FAR, which causes the FRR—the number of authorized persons disallowed access—to increase.
texts.text: The crossover rate is sometimes referred to as equal error rate. In a very sensitive system, it may be desirable to minimize the number of false accepts—the number of unauthorized persons allowed access. To do this, the system is tuned to be more sensitive with a lower FAR, which causes the FRR—the number of authorized persons disallowed access—to increase.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. As the sensitivity of the biometric system is adjusted, the FRR and FAR change inversely: At one point, the two values intersect and are equal. This condition creates the crossover error rate, which is a measure of the system accuracy. Lower than the crossover error rate will create too. high a FAR for a high-security data center.
texts.text: As the sensitivity of the biometric system is adjusted, the FRR and FAR change inversely: At one point, the two values intersect and are equal. This condition creates the crossover error rate, which is a measure of the system accuracy. Lower than the crossover error rate will create too. high a FAR for a high-security data center.

texts.text: An enterprise is implementing intrusion protection in its demilitarized zone (DMZ). Which of the following steps is necessary to make sure that the intrusion prevention system (IPS) can view all traffic in the DMZ?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Ensure that intrusion prevention is placed in front of the firewall.
texts.text: Ensure that intrusion prevention is placed in front of the firewall.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Ensure that all devices that are connected can easily see the IPS in the network.
texts.text: Ensure that all devices that are connected can easily see the IPS in the network.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Ensure that all encrypted traffic is decrypted prior to being processed by the IPS.
texts.text: Ensure that all encrypted traffic is decrypted prior to being processed by the IPS.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Ensure that traffic to all devices is mirrored to the IPS.
texts.text: Ensure that traffic to all devices is mirrored to the IPS.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. An intrusion prevention system (IPS) placed in front of the firewall will almost certainly continuously detect potential attacks, creating endless false-positives and directing the firewall to block many sites needlessly. Most of actual attacks would be intercepted by the firewall in any case.
texts.text: An intrusion prevention system (IPS) placed in front of the firewall will almost certainly continuously detect potential attacks, creating endless false-positives and directing the firewall to block many sites needlessly. Most of actual attacks would be intercepted by the firewall in any case.

texts.orig: B. All connected devices do not need to see the IPS.

The encryption should be terminated at a hardware Secure Sockets Layer accelerator or virtual private network server to allow all traffic to be monitored.

The encryption should be terminated at a hardware Secure Sockets Layer accelerator or virtual private network server to allow all traffic to be monitored.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Traffic to all devices is not mirrored to the IPS.

texts.orig: 79. Which of the following mechanisms is the MOST secure way to implement a secure wireless network?
texts.text: Which of the following mechanisms is the MOST secure way to implement a secure wireless network?

texts.orig: A. Filter media access control addresses.
texts.text: Filter media access control addresses.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Use a Wi-Fi Protected Access protocol.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Media access control (MAC) address filtering by itself is not a good security mechanism because allowed MAC addresses can be easily sniffed and then spoofed to get into the network.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Wi-Fi Protected Access (WPA2) protocol is currently one of the most secure authentication and encryption protocols for mainstream wireless products.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Wired Equivalent Privacy (WEP) is no longer a secure encryption mechanism for wireless communications. The WEP key can be easily broken within minutes using widely available software. Once the WEP key is obtained, all communications of every other wireless client are exposed.

texts.orig: 87. Which of the following control measures BEST addresses integrity?
texts.text: Which of the following control measures BEST addresses integrity?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Nonrepudiation
texts.text: Nonrepudiation

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Time stamps

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Nonrepudiation is a control technique that addresses the integrity of information by ensuring that the originator of a message or transaction cannot repudiate (deny or reject) the message, so the message or transaction can be considered authorized, authentic and valid.
texts.text: Nonrepudiation is a control technique that addresses the integrity of information by ensuring that the originator of a message or transaction cannot repudiate (deny or reject) the message, so the message or transaction can be considered authorized, authentic and valid.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Using time stamps is a control that addresses only one component of message integrity.
texts.text: Using time stamps is a control that addresses only one component of message integrity.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Biometric scanning is a control that addresses access.
texts.text: Biometric scanning is a control that addresses access.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Encryption is a control that addresses confidentiality; it may be an element of a data integrity scheme, but it is not sufficient to achieve the same level of integrity as the set of measures used to ensure nonrepudiation.
texts.text: Encryption is a control that addresses confidentiality; it may be an element of a data integrity scheme, but it is not sufficient to achieve the same level of integrity as the set of measures used to ensure nonrepudiation.

texts.orig: B. There is a chance that fraud can be committed because the administrator can manipulate the database server. The administrator may alter database transactions and then erase the log. texts.orig: 100. The MOST important consideration when determining how a control policy is implemented is:
texts.text: The MOST important consideration when determining how a control policy is implemented is:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. the risk of compromise.
texts.text: the risk of compromise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. the safety of personnel.
texts.text: the safety of personnel.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. the mean time between failures.
texts.text: the mean time between failures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. the nature of a threat.
texts.text: the nature of a threat.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The risk of compromise is a major consideration in the level of protection required, but not at the expense of safety. Only in very rare circumstances does risk of compromise outweigh life safety, and even then it is the risk to a larger population that justifies a fail secure configuration.
texts.text: The risk of compromise is a major consideration in the level of protection required, but not at the expense of safety. Only in very rare circumstances does risk of compromise outweigh life safety, and even then it is the risk to a larger population that justifies a fail secure configuration.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Safety of personnel is always the first consideration. For example, even if a data center has highly confidential data, failure of physical access controls should not fail closed and prevent emergency exit, Only in very rare circumstances does risk of compromise outweigh life safety, and even then it is the risk to a larger population that justifies a fail secure configuration.
texts.text: Safety of personnel is always the first consideration. For example, even if a data center has highly confidential data, failure of physical access controls should not fail closed and prevent emergency exit, Only in very rare circumstances does risk of compromise outweigh life safety, and even then it is the risk to a larger population that justifies a fail secure configuration.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The mean time between failure is a consideration for technical or mechanical controls and must be considered from a safety perspective.
texts.text: The mean time between failure is a consideration for technical or mechanical controls and must be considered from a safety perspective.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The nature of a threat is a consideration for the type and strength of controls.
texts.text: The nature of a threat is a consideration for the type and strength of controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Use a deterrent control.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Reduce exposure.

texts.orig: C. Use a compensating control.
texts.text: Use a compensating control.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Using a deterrent control will have only a limited effect on the possibility of compromise.
texts.text: Using a deterrent control will have only a limited effect on the possibility of compromise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Reducing exposure reduces the probability that a risk can be exploited.
texts.text: Reducing exposure reduces the probability that a risk can be exploited.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Using a compensating control will serve to limit impact, but do nothing to prevent exploitation.
texts.text: Using a compensating control will serve to limit impact, but do nothing to prevent exploitation.
