texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 321. An information security manager has received complaints from senior management about the level of security delivered by a third-party service provider. The service provider is a long-standing vendor providing services based on a service agreement that has been renewed regularly without much change over the last four years. Which of the following actions is the FIRST one the information security manager should take in this situation?
texts.text: An information security manager has received complaints from senior management about the level of security delivered by a third-party service provider. The service provider is a long-standing vendor providing services based on a service agreement that has been renewed regularly without much change over the last four years. Which of the following actions is the FIRST one the information security manager should take in this situation?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Ensure that security requirements in the service agreement meet current business requirements.
texts.text: Ensure that security requirements in the service agreement meet current business requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Conduct a formal assessment of the vendor's capability to deliver security services.
texts.text: Conduct a formal assessment of the vendor's capability to deliver security services.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Review security metrics to determine whether the vendor is meeting the terms of the service agreement.
texts.text: Review security metrics to determine whether the vendor is meeting the terms of the service agreement.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Automate the incident reporting process to ensure timely reporting and monitoring.
texts.text: Automate the incident reporting process to ensure timely reporting and monitoring.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Because the service agreement has not been significantly revised in four years, it is entirely likely that the vendor is delivering exactly what was purchased and that the disappointment shown by senior management is the result of the agreement not reflecting current business requirements.
texts.text: Because the service agreement has not been significantly revised in four years, it is entirely likely that the vendor is delivering exactly what was purchased and that the disappointment shown by senior management is the result of the agreement not reflecting current business requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. If the vendor has committed to a level of security services that metrics indicate are consistently not being met, it may be worthwhile to conduct a formal assessment of the vendor's capabilities to determine whether a new vendor is needed. However, knowing how what was contracted aligns with business requirements needs to be the first step.
texts.text: If the vendor has committed to a level of security services that metrics indicate are consistently not being met, it may be worthwhile to conduct a formal assessment of the vendor's capabilities to determine whether a new vendor is needed. However, knowing how what was contracted aligns with business requirements needs to be the first step.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Knowing whether the vendor is meeting the terms of the agreement is actionable only after the information security manager is certain that the terms of the agreement align with the business requirements of the company.
texts.text: Knowing whether the vendor is meeting the terms of the agreement is actionable only after the information security manager is certain that the terms of the agreement align with the business requirements of the company.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Automation of the incident reporting process to ensure timely reporting and monitoring is only a reporting mechanism and does not resolve the issues faced.
texts.text: Automation of the incident reporting process to ensure timely reporting and monitoring is only a reporting mechanism and does not resolve the issues faced.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 322. How should an information security manager proceed when selecting a public cloud vendor to provide outsourced infrastructure and software?
texts.text: How should an information security manager proceed when selecting a public cloud vendor to provide outsourced infrastructure and software?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Insist on strict service level agreements to guarantee application availability.
texts.text: Insist on strict service level agreements to guarantee application availability.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Verify that the vendor's security posture meets the enterprise's requirements.
texts.text: Verify that the vendor's security posture meets the enterprise's requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Update the enterprise's security policies to reflect the vendor agreement.
texts.text: Update the enterprise's security policies to reflect the vendor agreement.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Consult a third party to provide an audit report to assess the vendor's security program.
texts.text: Consult a third party to provide an audit report to assess the vendor's security program.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Agreements that address availability do not address other aspects of the enterprise's security policy.
texts.text: Agreements that address availability do not address other aspects of the enterprise's security policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. An enterprise defines its security policies with its business risk in mind. Changing internal policy requirements to reflect what a vendor can deliver may not be sufficient and could raise risk to the enterprise making it an inappropriate approach.
texts.text: An enterprise defines its security policies with its business risk in mind. Changing internal policy requirements to reflect what a vendor can deliver may not be sufficient and could raise risk to the enterprise making it an inappropriate approach.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. When considering a cloud implementation, an information security manager must verify that a chosen vendor will meet the enterprise's security requirements.
texts.text: When considering a cloud implementation, an information security manager must verify that a chosen vendor will meet the enterprise's security requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Third-party audit reports are snapshots that tell what was true at a particular time and address only those items that were within the audit scope. Each enterprise has its own security policy considerations, and verification with the vendor should be accomplished with the enterprise's specific considerations and requirements in mind.
texts.text: Third-party audit reports are snapshots that tell what was true at a particular time and address only those items that were within the audit scope. Each enterprise has its own security policy considerations, and verification with the vendor should be accomplished with the enterprise's specific considerations and requirements in mind.

texts.orig: 323. Which of the following approaches is the BEST for designing role-based access controls?
texts.text: Which of the following approaches is the BEST for designing role-based access controls?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Create a matrix of work functions.
texts.text: Create a matrix of work functions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Apply persistent data labels.
texts.text: Apply persistent data labels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Enable multifactor authentication.
texts.text: Enable multifactor authentication.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Use individual logon scripts.
texts.text: Use individual logon scripts.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A matrix that documents the functions associated with particular kinds of work, typically referred to as a segregation of duties matrix, shows which roles are required or need various permissions.
texts.text: A matrix that documents the functions associated with particular kinds of work, typically referred to as a segregation of duties matrix, shows which roles are required or need various permissions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Persistent data labels apply to mandatory access control environments where permissions are brokered by the classification levels of objects themselves. They do not factor into role-based access controls.
texts.text: Persistent data labels apply to mandatory access control environments where permissions are brokered by the classification levels of objects themselves. They do not factor into role-based access controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Multifactor authentication deals with how users authenticate their identities, which helps to ensure that people are who they claim to be. It does not determine the permissions that they are assigned, particularly in a role-based access control model, where permissions are assigned to roles rather than individual users.
texts.text: Multifactor authentication deals with how users authenticate their identities, which helps to ensure that people are who they claim to be. It does not determine the permissions that they are assigned, particularly in a role-based access control model, where permissions are assigned to roles rather than individual users.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Using automated logon scripts is practical in some environments, but assigning permissions to individual accounts is contrary to the intent of role-based access controls.
texts.text: Using automated logon scripts is practical in some environments, but assigning permissions to individual accounts is contrary to the intent of role-based access controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. To understand the risk of technology and its contribution to security objectives
texts.text: To understand the risk of technology and its contribution to security objectives

texts.text: To assist and advise on the acquisition and deployment of information technology

texts.text: Which of the following conditions is MOST likely to require that a corporate standard be modified?

texts.orig: A. The standard does not conform to procedures.
texts.text: The standard does not conform to procedures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. IT staff does not understand the standard.
texts.text: IT staff does not understand the standard.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The standard is inconsistent with guidelines.
texts.text: The standard is inconsistent with guidelines.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Control objectives are not being met.
texts.text: Control objectives are not being met.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. If a procedure does not meet the standard, the procedure must be changed, not the standard.
texts.text: If a procedure does not meet the standard, the procedure must be changed, not the standard.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. IT staff not understanding the standard may require clarification and/or training.
texts.text: IT staff not understanding the standard may require clarification and/or training.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. If conformance with the standard does not achieve control objectives, the standard requires modification.
texts.text: If conformance with the standard does not achieve control objectives, the standard requires modification.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Inconsistencies with the guidelines require that the guidelines be changed to conform to the standard.
texts.text: Inconsistencies with the guidelines require that the guidelines be changed to conform to the standard.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 329. The protection of sensitive data stored at a third-party location requires:
texts.text: The protection of sensitive data stored at a third-party location requires:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. assurances that the third party will comply with the requirements of the contract.
texts.text: assurances that the third party will comply with the requirements of the contract.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. commitments to completion of periodic independent security audits.
texts.text: commitments to completion of periodic independent security audits.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. security awareness training and background checks of all third-party employees.
texts.text: security awareness training and background checks of all third-party employees.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. periodic review of third-party contracts and policies to ensure compliance.
texts.text: periodic review of third-party contracts and policies to ensure compliance.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. When storing data with a third party, the ownership and responsibility for the adequate protection of the data remains with the outsourcing enterprise. The outsourcing enterprise should have measures in place to provide assurance of compliance with the terms of the contract, which should be written on the basis of the organizational risk appetite.
texts.text: When storing data with a third party, the ownership and responsibility for the adequate protection of the data remains with the outsourcing enterprise. The outsourcing enterprise should have measures in place to provide assurance of compliance with the terms of the contract, which should be written on the basis of the organizational risk appetite.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Independent security audits are one assurance mechanism that an enterprise may use to verify compliance with contractual requirements, but whether they are appropriate is situational and based on the organizational risk appetite.
texts.text: Independent security audits are one assurance mechanism that an enterprise may use to verify compliance with contractual requirements, but whether they are appropriate is situational and based on the organizational risk appetite.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Awareness training and background checks are assurance mechanisms but may or may not be appropriate or important in all cases.
texts.text: Awareness training and background checks are assurance mechanisms but may or may not be appropriate or important in all cases.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Review of contracts and policies is important, but it does not assure compliance.
texts.text: Review of contracts and policies is important, but it does not assure compliance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 330. A new business application requires deviation from the standard configuration of the operating system (OS). Which of the following steps should the security manager take FIRST?
texts.text: A new business application requires deviation from the standard configuration of the operating system (OS). Which of the following steps should the security manager take FIRST?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Contact the vendor to modify the application.
texts.text: Contact the vendor to modify the application.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Assess risk and identify compensating controls.
texts.text: Assess risk and identify compensating controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Approve an exception to the policy to meet business needs.
texts.text: Approve an exception to the policy to meet business needs.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Review and update the OS baseline configuration.
texts.text: Review and update the OS baseline configuration.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The security manager would contact the vendor to modify the application only after assessing the risk and identifying compensating controls.
texts.text: The security manager would contact the vendor to modify the application only after assessing the risk and identifying compensating controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Before approving any exception, the security manager should first check for compensating controls and assess the possible risk due to deviation.
texts.text: Before approving any exception, the security manager should first check for compensating controls and assess the possible risk due to deviation.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The security manager may make a case for deviation from the policy, but this would be based on a risk assessment and compensating controls. The deviation itself would be approved in accordance with a defined process.
texts.text: The security manager may make a case for deviation from the policy, but this would be based on a risk assessment and compensating controls. The deviation itself would be approved in accordance with a defined process.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Updating the baseline configuration is not associated with requests for deviations.
texts.text: Updating the baseline configuration is not associated with requests for deviations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 331. Which of the following training mechanisms is the MOST effective means of promoting an organizational security culture?
texts.text: Which of the following training mechanisms is the MOST effective means of promoting an organizational security culture?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Choose a subset of influential people to promote the benefits of the security program.
texts.text: Choose a subset of influential people to promote the benefits of the security program.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Hold structured training in small groups on an annual basis.
texts.text: Hold structured training in small groups on an annual basis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Require each employee to complete a self-paced training module once per year.
texts.text: Require each employee to complete a self-paced training module once per year.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Deliver training to all employees across the enterprise via streaming video.
texts.text: Deliver training to all employees across the enterprise via streaming video.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Certain people are either individually inclined or required by their positions to have greater interest in promoting security than others. By selecting these people and offering them broad, diverse opportunities for security education, they are able to act as ambassadors to their respective teams and departments, imparting a gradual and significant change in an organizational culture toward better security.
texts.text: Certain people are either individually inclined or required by their positions to have greater interest in promoting security than others. By selecting these people and offering them broad, diverse opportunities for security education, they are able to act as ambassadors to their respective teams and departments, imparting a gradual and significant change in an organizational culture toward better security.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Structured training rarely aligns with the interests of individual employees when chosen at random to fill a small group setting.
texts.text: Structured training rarely aligns with the interests of individual employees when chosen at random to fill a small group setting.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Computer-based training is a common approach to annual information awareness, but there is limited evidence that employees retain the information or adopt it into their regular activities.
texts.text: Computer-based training is a common approach to annual information awareness, but there is limited evidence that employees retain the information or adopt it into their regular activities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Streaming-video webinars are among the least effective means of presenting information, requiring very little interaction from end users.
texts.text: Streaming-video webinars are among the least effective means of presenting information, requiring very little interaction from end users.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 332. Which of the following challenges associated with information security documentation is MOST likely to affect a large, established enterprise?
texts.text: Which of the following challenges associated with information security documentation is MOST likely to affect a large, established enterprise?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Standards change more slowly than the environment.
texts.text: Standards change more slowly than the environment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Policies change faster than they can be distributed.
texts.text: Policies change faster than they can be distributed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Procedures are ignored to meet operational requirements.
texts.text: Procedures are ignored to meet operational requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Policies remain unchanged for long periods of time.
texts.text: Policies remain unchanged for long periods of time.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Large, established enterprises tend to have numerous layers of review and approval associated with changes to standards. These review mechanisms are likely to be outpaced by changes in technology and the risk environment.
texts.text: Large, established enterprises tend to have numerous layers of review and approval associated with changes to standards. These review mechanisms are likely to be outpaced by changes in technology and the risk environment.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Policies are meant to reflect strategic goals and objectives. In small or immature enterprises, the policy model may be poorly implemented, resulting in rapid changes to policies that are treated more like standards, but this situation is unlikely to arise in a large, established enterprise.
texts.text: Policies are meant to reflect strategic goals and objectives. In small or immature enterprises, the policy model may be poorly implemented, resulting in rapid changes to policies that are treated more like standards, but this situation is unlikely to arise in a large, established enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Large, established enterprises typically have formal training programs and internal controls that keep activities substantially in line with published procedures.
texts.text: Large, established enterprises typically have formal training programs and internal controls that keep activities substantially in line with published procedures.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Although policies should be subject to periodic review and not be regarded as static, properly written policies should require significant changes only when there are substantial changes in strategic goals and objectives. It is reasonable that a large, established enterprise would experience policy changes only rarely.
texts.text: Although policies should be subject to periodic review and not be regarded as static, properly written policies should require significant changes only when there are substantial changes in strategic goals and objectives. It is reasonable that a large, established enterprise would experience policy changes only rarely.

texts.orig: 333. In a financial institution, under which of the following circumstances will policies MOST likely need modification?
texts.text: In a financial institution, under which of the following circumstances will policies MOST likely need modification?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Current access controls have been insufficient to prevent a series of serious network breaches.
texts.text: Current access controls have been insufficient to prevent a series of serious network breaches.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The information security manager has determined that compliance with configuration standards is inadequate.
texts.text: The information security manager has determined that compliance with configuration standards is inadequate.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The results of an audit have identified a going concern issue with the enterprise.
texts.text: The results of an audit have identified a going concern issue with the enterprise.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Management has mandated compliance with a newly enacted set of information security requirements.
texts.text: Management has mandated compliance with a newly enacted set of information security requirements.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header

texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Necessary modifications to access controls are most likely going to be reflected in standards, not policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Compliance with existing standards is not likely to require a policy change; better enforcement may be needed.
texts.text: Compliance with existing standards is not likely to require a policy change; better enforcement may be needed.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. If the viability of the enterprise is in doubt (going concern), it is not likely that a change in policy will solve the problem.
texts.text: If the viability of the enterprise is in doubt (going concern), it is not likely that a change in policy will solve the problem.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. A new set of regulations requiring significant changes to the information security program most likely will be reflected in modifications of policy.
texts.text: A new set of regulations requiring significant changes to the information security program most likely will be reflected in modifications of policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 334. Which of the following tools should a newly hired information securitymanager review to gain an understanding of how effectively the current set of information security projects are managed?
texts.text: Which of the following tools should a newly hired information securitymanager review to gain an understanding of how effectively the current set of information security projects are managed?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A project database
texts.text: A project database

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A project portfolio database
texts.text: A project portfolio database

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Policy documents
texts.text: Policy documents

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. A program management office
texts.text: A program management office

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A project database may contain information for one specific project and updates to various parameters pertaining to the current status of that single project.
texts.text: A project database may contain information for one specific project and updates to various parameters pertaining to the current status of that single project.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A project portfolio database is the basis for project portfolio management. It includes project data such as owner, schedules, objectives, project type, status and cost. Project portfolio management requires specific project portfolio reports.
texts.text: A project portfolio database is the basis for project portfolio management. It includes project data such as owner, schedules, objectives, project type, status and cost. Project portfolio management requires specific project portfolio reports.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Policy documents on project management set direction for the design, development, implementation and monitoring of the project.
texts.text: Policy documents on project management set direction for the design, development, implementation and monitoring of the project.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. A program management office is the team that oversees the delivery of the project portfolio. Review of the office may provide meaningful insights into the skill set and organizational structure but not on how effectively the current set of information security projects is managed.
texts.text: A program management office is the team that oversees the delivery of the project portfolio. Review of the office may provide meaningful insights into the skill set and organizational structure but not on how effectively the current set of information security projects is managed.

texts.orig: 335. What is the MAIN objective for developing an information security program?
texts.text: What is the MAIN objective for developing an information security program?

texts.orig: A. To create the information security policy
texts.text: To create the information security policy

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. To maximize system uptime
texts.text: To maximize system uptime

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. To develop strong controls
texts.text: To develop strong controls

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. To implement the strategy
texts.text: To implement the strategy

texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The policy should not be written for its own sake. To be effective, the policy must address the threat and risn s s s    t l le:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 336. An information security manager has implemented an automated process to compare physical access using swipe cards operated by the physical security department with logical access in the single sign-on (SSO) system. What is the MOST likely use for this information?
texts.text: An information security manager has implemented an automated process to compare physical access using swipe cards operated by the physical security department with logical access in the single sign-on (SSO) system. What is the MOST likely use for this information?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Monitoring a key risk indicator
texts.text: Monitoring a key risk indicator

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Determining whether staff is piggybacking
texts.text: Determining whether staff is piggybacking

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Overseeing the physical security department
texts.text: Overseeing the physical security department

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Evaluating the SSO process
texts.text: Evaluating the SSO process

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Discrepancies between physical and logical access can occur for a variety of reasons, but all are indications that something is wrong and risk is elevated. Discrepancies could indicate piggybacking, shared passwords or attempts at unauthorized access, and therefore, this monitoring can serve as a key risk indicator (KRI).
texts.text: Discrepancies between physical and logical access can occur for a variety of reasons, but all are indications that something is wrong and risk is elevated. Discrepancies could indicate piggybacking, shared passwords or attempts at unauthorized access, and therefore, this monitoring can serve as a key risk indicator (KRI).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Potential piggybacking can be flagged if more individuals log in from within the network than physically enter the facility; however, this is just one KRI.
texts.text: Potential piggybacking can be flagged if more individuals log in from within the network than physically enter the facility; however, this is just one KRI.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Although this information could indicate that the physical access control is not functioning properly, the responsibility for oversight of the physical security department is not usually a function of the information security manager.
texts.text: Although this information could indicate that the physical access control is not functioning properly, the responsibility for oversight of the physical security department is not usually a function of the information security manager.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Comparing physical access and logical access is not an effective way to monitor the single sign-on (SSO) system, and there are other methods more specific and useful for this purpose.
texts.text: Comparing physical access and logical access is not an effective way to monitor the single sign-on (SSO) system, and there are other methods more specific and useful for this purpose.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 339. The relationship between policies and corporate standards can BEST be described by which of the following associations?
texts.text: The relationship between policies and corporate standards can BEST be described by which of the following associations?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Standards and policies have only an indirect relationship.
texts.text: Standards and policies have only an indirect relationship.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Standards provide a detailed description of the meaning of a policy.
texts.text: Standards provide a detailed description of the meaning of a policy.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Standards provide direction on achieving compliance with policy intent.
texts.text: Standards provide direction on achieving compliance with policy intent.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Standards can exist without a relationship to any particular policy.
texts.text: Standards can exist without a relationship to any particular policy.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. In most cases, there is a direct relationship between policy and corporate standards.
texts.text: In most cases, there is a direct relationship between policy and corporate standards.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Corporate standards generally do not provide details on the meaning of policy, rather on the acceptable limits needed to comply with policy intent.
texts.text: Corporate standards generally do not provide details on the meaning of policy, rather on the acceptable limits needed to comply with policy intent.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Corporate standards set the allowable limits and boundaries for people, processes and technology as an expression of policy intent and, therefore, provide direction on policy compliance.
texts.text: Corporate standards set the allowable limits and boundaries for people, processes and technology as an expression of policy intent and, therefore, provide direction on policy compliance.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. It would be a poor practice to have corporate standards not directly expressing the intent of a particular policy. To the extent that they exist, they should rely on an implicit policy.
texts.text: It would be a poor practice to have corporate standards not directly expressing the intent of a particular policy. To the extent that they exist, they should rely on an implicit policy.

texts.orig: 340. A person working at a bank receives a call on a voice-over Internet protocol line from a persón claiming to be an employee of the bank at another branch office. He is requesting customer information. The FIRST action to take when receiving this type of call is to:
texts.text: A person working at a bank receives a call on a voice-over Internet protocol line from a persón claiming to be an employee of the bank at another branch office. He is requesting customer information. The FIRST action to take when receiving this type of call is to:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. obtain the email address of the caller and have the recipient transmit the information using message encryption.
texts.text: obtain the email address of the caller and have the recipient transmit the information using message encryption.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. advise the employee who received the call to hang up and then return the call to the other branch using the number in the office phone directory.
texts.text: advise the employee who received the call to hang up and then return the call to the other branch using the number in the office phone directory.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. pose business-related questions to the caller, and if a proper reply is received, the recipient may forward the information to the caller.
texts.text: pose business-related questions to the caller, and if a proper reply is received, the recipient may forward the information to the caller.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. ask the person to call back later and notify regulatory officers of a possible fraud attempt.
texts.text: ask the person to call back later and notify regulatory officers of a possible fraud attempt.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Sensitive information should not be sent to a third party that has not been validated even if encryption is used, because the enterprise cannot guarantee that the recipient will be unable to decipher information in a time period during which the information can still be used.
texts.text: Sensitive information should not be sent to a third party that has not been validated even if encryption is used, because the enterprise cannot guarantee that the recipient will be unable to decipher information in a time period during which the information can still be used.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. If the call recipient suspects any chance of social engineering over the phone, the callback option is bue       s e   e d    at phone number listed in the office phone directory. The recipient should not use a phone number or email address provided by the caller. Once the legitimacy of the call has been reasonably verified, the information may be transmitted using message encryption. Even after voice verification, it is essential that encryption be used because voice verification might be subject to additional attacks (e.g., man-in-the-middle).
texts.text: If the call recipient suspects any chance of social engineering over the phone, the callback option is bue       s e   e d    at phone number listed in the office phone directory. The recipient should not use a phone number or email address provided by the caller. Once the legitimacy of the call has been reasonably verified, the information may be transmitted using message encryption. Even after voice verification, it is essential that encryption be used because voice verification might be subject to additional attacks (e.g., man-in-the-middle).

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Even when there is a strong suspicion of fraud, the recipient should not indicate this to the caller over the phone. Instead, the recipient should hang up and call back using the phone number from the office phone directory.
texts.text: Even when there is a strong suspicion of fraud, the recipient should not indicate this to the caller over the phone. Instead, the recipient should hang up and call back using the phone number from the office phone directory.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. The person attempting social engineering will attempt to pass business (or non-business) related questions to the caller. If proper answers are obtained, the recipient will continue the conversation. A caller who feels uneasy will have the control to end the conversation. Because this technique gives the attacker control of the conversation, it is not the best answer.

texts.text: Which of the following reasons is MOST likely why an enterprise has decided to outsource intrusion detection seivices?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. As a response to audit recommendations
texts.text: As a response to audit recommendations

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Due to the complexity of interpreting attacks
texts.text: Due to the complexity of interpreting attacks

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. As a result of a cost-benefit analysis
texts.text: As a result of a cost-benefit analysis

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Due to lack of competent staff
texts.text: Due to lack of competent staff

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Audit recommendations may lead to a cost-benefit analysis, but generally do not direct a particular approach to solving an identified problem.
texts.text: Audit recommendations may lead to a cost-benefit analysis, but generally do not direct a particular approach to solving an identified problem.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: Technology for intrusion detection that reduces complexity to manage the levels is available but may not be cost-effective.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A cost-benefit analysis addresses the trade-offs between in-house and outsourced services. If outsourcing is chosen, it is generally chosen on the basis of cost-effectiveness.
texts.text: A cost-benefit analysis addresses the trade-offs between in-house and outsourced services. If outsourcing is chosen, it is generally chosen on the basis of cost-effectiveness.

texts.text: Hiring staff with the proper skill set for intrusion detection is generally possible but may not be costeffective.

texts.orig: 344. What is the initial step that an information security manager would take during the requirements gathering phase of an IT project to avoid project failure?
texts.text: What is the initial step that an information security manager would take during the requirements gathering phase of an IT project to avoid project failure?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Develop a comprehensive methodology that defines and documents project needs.
texts.text: Develop a comprehensive methodology that defines and documents project needs.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Ensure that the business problem is clearly understood before working on the solution.
texts.text: Ensure that the business problem is clearly understood before working on the solution.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Build security requirements into the design of the system with consideration of enterprise security needs.
texts.text: Build security requirements into the design of the system with consideration of enterprise security needs.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Create a project plan based on the principles of agile development methodology.
texts.text: Create a project plan based on the principles of agile development methodology.

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.orig: A. Developing a methodology is a step separate from defining requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. The question relates to requirements-gathering phase of the project, not the design phase. Therefore, it would be too early to start building the requirement into the design.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. The key to successful requirements gathering is to focus initially on the business problem before trying to develop a solution. Otherwise, the solution may address the wrong problem.
texts.text: The key to successful requirements gathering is to focus initially on the business problem before trying to develop a solution. Otherwise, the solution may address the wrong problem.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. An agile development methodology first requires the determination of business requirements.
texts.text: An agile development methodology first requires the determination of business requirements.

texts.orig: 351. An advantage of using a cloud computing solution over a locally hosted solution is:
texts.text: An advantage of using a cloud computing solution over a locally hosted solution is:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. the ability to obtain storage and bandwidth on demand.
texts.text: the ability to obtain storage and bandwidth on demand.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. reduced requirements for training of users and managers.
texts.text: reduced requirements for training of users and managers.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. increased security as a result of encrópting data in transit.
texts.text: increased security as a result of encrópting data in transit.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: the opportunity to control changes to applications and data.

texts.label: list_item

A project manager is developing a developer portal and requests that the security manager assign a public Internet Protocol address so that it can be accessed by in-house staff and by external consultants outside the enterprise's local area network. What should the security manager do FIRST?
texts.text: A project manager is developing a developer portal and requests that the security manager assign a public Internet Protocol address so that it can be accessed by in-house staff and by external consultants outside the enterprise's local area network. What should the security manager do FIRST?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Understand the business requirements of the developer portal.
texts.text: Understand the business requirements of the developer portal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Perform a vulnerability assessment of the developer portal.
texts.text: Perform a vulnerability assessment of the developer portal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Install an intrusion detection system.
texts.text: Install an intrusion detection system.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Obtain a signed nondisclosure agreement from the external consultants before allowing external access to the server.
texts.text: Obtain a signed nondisclosure agreement from the external consultants before allowing external access to the server.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The information security manager cannot make an informed decision about the request without first understanding the business requirements of the developer portal.
texts.text: The information security manager cannot make an informed decision about the request without first understanding the business requirements of the developer portal.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Performing a vulnerability assessment of developer portal is prudent but it should follow understanding the requirements.
texts.text: Performing a vulnerability assessment of developer portal is prudent but it should follow understanding the requirements.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Installing an intrusion detection system may be useful but not as essential as understanding the requirements.
texts.text: Installing an intrusion detection system may be useful but not as essential as understanding the requirements.

texts.orig: 356. A mission-critical system has been identified as having an administrative system account with attributes that prevent locking and change of privileges and name. Which would be the BEST approach to prevent a successful brute force attack of the account?
texts.text: A mission-critical system has been identified as having an administrative system account with attributes that prevent locking and change of privileges and name. Which would be the BEST approach to prevent a successful brute force attack of the account?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Prevent the system from being accessed remotely.
texts.text: Prevent the system from being accessed remotely.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Create a strong random password.
texts.text: Create a strong random password.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Ask for a vendor patch.
texts.text: Ask for a vendor patch.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Track usage of the account by audit trails.
texts.text: Track usage of the account by audit trails.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Preventing the system from being accessed remotely is not always an option in mission-critical systems and still leaves local access risk.
texts.text: Preventing the system from being accessed remotely is not always an option in mission-critical systems and still leaves local access risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Creating a strong random password reduces the risk of a successful brute force attack by exponentially increasing the time required.
texts.text: Creating a strong random password reduces the risk of a successful brute force attack by exponentially increasing the time required.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Vendor patches are not always available.
texts.text: Vendor patches are not always available.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Tracking usage is a detective control and will not prevent an attack.
texts.text: Tracking usage is a detective control and will not prevent an attack.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 357. Business management is finalizing the contents of a segregation of duties matrix to be loaded in a purchase order system. Which of the following should the information security manager recommend in order to BEST improve the effectiveness of the matrix?
texts.text: Business management is finalizing the contents of a segregation of duties matrix to be loaded in a purchase order system. Which of the following should the information security manager recommend in order to BEST improve the effectiveness of the matrix?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Ensure approvers are aligned with the organizational chart
texts.text: Ensure approvers are aligned with the organizational chart

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Trace approvers' paths to eliminate routing deadlocks
texts.text: Trace approvers' paths to eliminate routing deadlocks

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Set triggers to go off in the event of exceptions
texts.text: Set triggers to go off in the event of exceptions

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Identify conflicts in the approvers' authority limits
texts.text: Identify conflicts in the approvers' authority limits

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The approver's structure in a purchase order system may not necessarily be in sync with the organizational structure. Depending on business requirements, modified hierarchy is acceptable purely in terms of approving certain transactions.
texts.text: The approver's structure in a purchase order system may not necessarily be in sync with the organizational structure. Depending on business requirements, modified hierarchy is acceptable purely in terms of approving certain transactions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. It is rare that the structure of an approver's routing path will end up with deadlocks. If a highly complicated approval structure is developed, something similar to deadlock may occur (e.g., it takes very long time until request is approved). Even so, it is unlikely that routing effectiveness becomes a primary driver for quality improvement.
texts.text: It is rare that the structure of an approver's routing path will end up with deadlocks. If a highly complicated approval structure is developed, something similar to deadlock may occur (e.g., it takes very long time until request is approved). Even so, it is unlikely that routing effectiveness becomes a primary driver for quality improvement.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Setting triggers to go off in the event of exceptions is a technical feature to be implemented inside the database. It is not relevant advice to be given to business management.
texts.text: Setting triggers to go off in the event of exceptions is a technical feature to be implemented inside the database. It is not relevant advice to be given to business management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. In order to make the segregation of duties matrix complete, it is best to ensure that no conflicts exist in approvers' authorities. If there are any, it will introduce a flaw in the control, resulting the successful execution of unauthorized transactions.
texts.text: In order to make the segregation of duties matrix complete, it is best to ensure that no conflicts exist in approvers' authorities. If there are any, it will introduce a flaw in the control, resulting the successful execution of unauthorized transactions.

texts.text: Active information security awareness programs PRIMARILY influence:

texts.text: acceptable risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. residual risk.
texts.text: residual risk.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. control objectives.
texts.text: control objectives.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The level of risk that an enterprise deems acceptable is a business decision. Controls, including active security awareness programs, are implemented to reduce risk to acceptable levels and do not influence what level of risk is acceptable.
texts.text: The level of risk that an enterprise deems acceptable is a business decision. Controls, including active security awareness programs, are implemented to reduce risk to acceptable levels and do not influence what level of risk is acceptable.

texts.orig: B. An information security awareness program is an administrative control that reduces.vulnerability, thereby yielding lower residual risk.

texts.orig: C. Security awareness may be a control objective, depending on the information security strategy of the enterprise, but such a program does not primarily influence the objectives of other controls.
texts.text: Security awareness may be a control objective, depending on the information security strategy of the enterprise, but such a program does not primarily influence the objectives of other controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Security awareness does not primarily influence business objectives.

texts.orig: 360. When considering outsourcing technical or business processes, one of the MAIN concerns of the information security manager is whether the third-party service provider will:
texts.text: When considering outsourcing technical or business processes, one of the MAIN concerns of the information security manager is whether the third-party service provider will:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. deliver a level of quality acceptable to the enterprise's established customer base.
texts.text: deliver a level of quality acceptable to the enterprise's established customer base.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. agree to service level agreements with penalties sufficient to offset potential losses.
texts.text: agree to service level agreements with penalties sufficient to offset potential losses.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. provide technical services at a lower cost than would be possible on an in-house basis.
texts.text: provide technical services at a lower cost than would be possible on an in-house basis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. meet the enterprise's security requirements on an ongoing and verifiable basis.
texts.text: meet the enterprise's security requirements on an ongoing and verifiable basis.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Quality assurance is an area of concern when dealing with third-party service providers, but it is not a primary focus of the information security manager.
texts.text: Quality assurance is an area of concern when dealing with third-party service providers, but it is not a primary focus of the information security manager.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Penalties written into service level agreements are a form of risk transfer (sharing) that may be appropriate for an enterprise's business objectives, but the sufficiency of such arrangeménts are not a primary focus of the information security manager.
texts.text: Penalties written into service level agreements are a form of risk transfer (sharing) that may be appropriate for an enterprise's business objectives, but the sufficiency of such arrangeménts are not a primary focus of the information security manager.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Reducing or controlling cost is typically one of the main reasons that enterprises choose to enter into thirdparty service agreements, but whether such agreements deliver their expected cost savings is not a primary focus of the information security manager.
texts.text: Reducing or controlling cost is typically one of the main reasons that enterprises choose to enter into thirdparty service agreements, but whether such agreements deliver their expected cost savings is not a primary focus of the information security manager.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. When an enterprise enters into an outsourcing agreement with a third-party service provider, the information security manager becomes responsible for ensuring that the provider adheres to the same security requirements as apply to the enterprise itself and that any variances are documented and presented to senior management for an appropriate risk response. The challenge of being able to assess a provider's security behaviors on an ongoing and verifiable basis is one of the main concerns of the information security manager in any outsourcing arrangement.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 361. IT management has standardized the Internet browser used within the enterprise. This practice is MOST effective in meeting which of the following objectives?
texts.text: IT management has standardized the Internet browser used within the enterprise. This practice is MOST effective in meeting which of the following objectives?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Prevent attacks designed to exploit known vulnerabilities.
texts.text: Prevent attacks designed to exploit known vulnerabilities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Ensure the subscription count is aligned with contract.
texts.text: Ensure the subscription count is aligned with contract.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Invalidate illegal browser script program development.
texts.text: Invalidate illegal browser script program development.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Guarantee compatibility with internal web-based applications.
texts.text: Guarantee compatibility with internal web-based applications.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: D is the correct answer.
texts.text: D is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Standardization of browsers within enterprises typically results in delays to upgrades and patching, making it more likely that the standardized browser will be susceptible to exploitation of known vulnerabilities.
texts.text: Standardization of browsers within enterprises typically results in delays to upgrades and patching, making it more likely that the standardized browser will be susceptible to exploitation of known vulnerabilities.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Controlling the version of the Internet browser used may not support the reconciliation between the subscription count and contract license number.
texts.text: Controlling the version of the Internet browser used may not support the reconciliation between the subscription count and contract license number.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Browser script development is generally not constrained by browser standardization. Information security managers seeking to prevent script execution would typically do so by standardizing configurations rather than versions.
texts.text: Browser script development is generally not constrained by browser standardization. Information security managers seeking to prevent script execution would typically do so by standardizing configurations rather than versions.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Internal web applications typically depend on particular versions of a web browser. Many enterprises choose to retain versions of their browsers beyond periods of support in order to maintain compatibility with their deployed applications.
texts.text: Internal web applications typically depend on particular versions of a web browser. Many enterprises choose to retain versions of their browsers beyond periods of support in order to maintain compatibility with their deployed applications.

texts.label: list_item

texts.orig: 363. Which of the following would be the BEST metric for an information security manager to provide to support a request to fund new controls?
texts.text: Which of the following would be the BEST metric for an information security manager to provide to support a request to fund new controls?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Adverse yearly incident trends
texts.text: Adverse yearly incident trends

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Audit findings of poor compliance
texts.text: Audit findings of poor compliance

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Results of a vulnerability scan
texts.text: Results of a vulnerability scan

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Increased external port scans
texts.text: Increased external port scans

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: A is the correct answer.
texts.text: A is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Security incidents occur because either a control failed or there was no control in place. Trends are a metric providing their own points of reference.
texts.text: Security incidents occur because either a control failed or there was no control in place. Trends are a metric providing their own points of reference.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Failures of compliance with existing controls are not likely to be solved by additional controls. Also, an audit finding absent any prior findings of compliance or other reference point is a measure, not a metric.
texts.text: Failures of compliance with existing controls are not likely to be solved by additional controls. Also, an audit finding absent any prior findings of compliance or other reference point is a measure, not a metric.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Port scans are common and generally will not support funding of new controls.
texts.text: Port scans are common and generally will not support funding of new controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Without knowing exposure, threat and potential impact, risk cannot be determined and will be poor support for new controls. Also, results of a vulnerability scan constitute a measure, not a metric.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 364. The MOST timely and effective approach to detecting nontechnical security violations in an enterprise is:
texts.text: The MOST timely and effective approach to detecting nontechnical security violations in an enterprise is:

texts.orig: A. the development of enterprise-wide communication channels.
texts.text: the development of enterprise-wide communication channels.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. periodic third-party auditing of incident reporting logs.
texts.text: periodic third-party auditing of incident reporting logs.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: an automated policy compliance monitoring system.

texts.label: list_item

texts.text: deployment of suggestion boxes throughout the enterprise.

texts.label: section_header

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Audits are one form of periodic reporting, but they are too infrequent for effective day-to-day information security management.
texts.text: Audits are one form of periodic reporting, but they are too infrequent for effective day-to-day information security management.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Automated policy compliance monitoring is useful for reporting IT-related processes but, by itself, is insufficient for nontechnical security violations.
texts.text: Automated policy compliance monitoring is useful for reporting IT-related processes but, by itself, is insufficient for nontechnical security violations.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Even if personnel could be persuaded to leave notes on policy violations in suggestion boxes, it would not be effective and is unlikely to be timely unless suggestions are collected daily.
texts.text: Even if personnel could be persuaded to leave notes on policy violations in suggestion boxes, it would not be effective and is unlikely to be timely unless suggestions are collected daily.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 366. Why is asset classification important to a successful information security program?
texts.text: Why is asset classification important to a successful information security program?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. It determines the priority and extent of risk mitigation efforts.
texts.text: It determines the priority and extent of risk mitigation efforts.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. It determines the amount of insurance needed in case of loss.
texts.text: It determines the amount of insurance needed in case of loss.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. It determines the appropriate level of protection to the asset.
texts.text: It determines the appropriate level of protection to the asset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. It determines how protection levels compare to peer enterprises.
texts.text: It determines how protection levels compare to peer enterprises.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Classification does not determine the priority and extent of the risk mitigation efforts; prioritization of risk mitigation efforts is generally based on risk analysis or a business impact analysis.
texts.text: Classification does not determine the priority and extent of the risk mitigation efforts; prioritization of risk mitigation efforts is generally based on risk analysis or a business impact analysis.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Classification is based on the value of the asset to the enterprise and helps establish the protection level in proportion to the value of the asset.
texts.text: Classification is based on the value of the asset to the enterprise and helps establish the protection level in proportion to the value of the asset.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Classification does not establish the amount of insurance needed; insurance is often not a viable option.
texts.text: Classification does not establish the amount of insurance needed; insurance is often not a viable option.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Classification schemes differ from enterprise to enterprise and are often not suitable for benchmarking.
texts.text: Classification schemes differ from enterprise to enterprise and are often not suitable for benchmarking.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 367. What is a reasonable approach to determine control effectiveness?
texts.text: What is a reasonable approach to determine control effectiveness?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Determine whether the control is preventive, detective or corrective.
texts.text: Determine whether the control is preventive, detective or corrective.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Review the control's capability of providing notification of failure.
texts.text: Review the control's capability of providing notification of failure.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Confirm the control's ability to meet intended objectives.
texts.text: Confirm the control's ability to meet intended objectives.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Assess and quantify the control's reliability.
texts.text: Assess and quantify the control's reliability.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. The type of control is not relevant.
texts.text: The type of control is not relevant.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Notification of failure is not determinative of control effectiveness.
texts.text: Notification of failure is not determinative of control effectiveness.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Control effectiveness requires a process to verify that the control process works as intended. Examples such as dual-control or dual-entry bookkeeping provide verification and assurance that the process operated as intended.
texts.text: Control effectiveness requires a process to verify that the control process works as intended. Examples such as dual-control or dual-entry bookkeeping provide verification and assurance that the process operated as intended.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Reliability is not an indication of control strength; weak controls can be highly reliable, even if they are ineffective controls.
texts.text: Reliability is not an indication of control strength; weak controls can be highly reliable, even if they are ineffective controls.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 371. Which of the following authentication methods prevents authentication replay?
texts.text: Which of the following authentication methods prevents authentication replay?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Password hash implementation
texts.text: Password hash implementation

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Challenge/response mechanism
texts.text: Challenge/response mechanism

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Wired equivalent privacy encryption usage
texts.text: Wired equivalent privacy encryption usage

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Hypertext Transfer Protocol basic authentication
texts.text: Hypertext Transfer Protocol basic authentication

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: B is the correct answer.
texts.text: B is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Capturing the authentication handshake and replaying it through the network will not work. Using hashes by itself will not prevent a replay.
texts.text: Capturing the authentication handshake and replaying it through the network will not work. Using hashes by itself will not prevent a replay.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A challenge/response mechanism prevents réplay attacks by sending a different random challenge in each authentication event. The response is linked to that challenge.
texts.text: A challenge/response mechanism prevents réplay attacks by sending a different random challenge in each authentication event. The response is linked to that challenge.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A wired equivalent privacy key will not prevent sniffing, but it will take the attacker longer to break the WEP key if they do not already have it. Therefore, it will not be able to prevent recording and replaying an authentication handshake.
texts.text: A wired equivalent privacy key will not prevent sniffing, but it will take the attacker longer to break the WEP key if they do not already have it. Therefore, it will not be able to prevent recording and replaying an authentication handshake.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Hypertext Transfer Protocol basic authentication is cleartext and has no mechanisms to prevent replay.
texts.text: Hypertext Transfer Protocol basic authentication is cleartext and has no mechanisms to prevent replay.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Provide a system-generated complex password by interoffice mail with 30 days expiration.
texts.text: Provide a system-generated complex password by interoffice mail with 30 days expiration.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Provide a temporary password over the telephone set for immediate expiration.
texts.text: Provide a temporary password over the telephone set for immediate expiration.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Require no password but force the user to set their own in 10 days.
texts.text: Require no password but force the user to set their own in 10 days.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Set initial password equal to the user ID with expiration in 30 days.
texts.text: Set initial password equal to the user ID with expiration in 30 days.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Documenting the password on paper is not the best method even if sent through interoffice mail—if the password is complex and difficult tò memorize, the user will likely keep the printed password, and this creates a security concern.
texts.text: Documenting the password on paper is not the best method even if sent through interoffice mail—if the password is complex and difficult tò memorize, the user will likely keep the printed password, and this creates a security concern.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A temporary password that will need to be changed upon.first logon is the best method because it is reset immediately and is replaced with the user's choice of password, which will make it easier for the user to remember. If it is given to the wrong person, the legitimate user will likely notify security if still unable to access the system; therefore, the security risk is low.
texts.text: A temporary password that will need to be changed upon.first logon is the best method because it is reset immediately and is replaced with the user's choice of password, which will make it easier for the user to remember. If it is given to the wrong person, the legitimate user will likely notify security if still unable to access the system; therefore, the security risk is low.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. Setting an account with no initial password is a security concern even if it is just for a few days.
texts.text: Setting an account with no initial password is a security concern even if it is just for a few days.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. This provides the greatest security threat because user IDs are typically known by both users and security staff, thus compromising access for up to 30 days.
texts.text: This provides the greatest security threat because user IDs are typically known by both users and security staff, thus compromising access for up to 30 days.
