texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Preventing access by system administrators provides no protection and does nothing to restore the system.
texts.text: Preventing access by system administrators provides no protection and does nothing to restore the system.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. Root access makes it possible to initiate changes that are difficult or impossible to locate, so undoing all changes is not an acceptable choice to resolve the issue.
texts.text: Root access makes it possible to initiate changes that are difficult or impossible to locate, so undoing all changes is not an acceptable choice to resolve the issue.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. If someone, or a malicious program, gains superuser privileges to a system without authorization, the enterprise never knows what the perpetrator or program has done to the system. The only way to assure the integrity of the system is to wipe it clean by either performing a low-level format on the hard disk or replacing it with a new one (usually after making a bit copy backup for the purpose of further analysis and to prevent the destruction of data that may not exist elsewhere) and then starting over again by reinstalling the operating system and applications using original media.

texts.label: list_item

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: 229. If a forensics copy of a hard drive is needed, which of the following would be the MOST defensible from a legal standpoint?
texts.text: If a forensics copy of a hard drive is needed, which of the following would be the MOST defensible from a legal standpoint?

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. A compressed copy of all contents of the hard drive
texts.text: A compressed copy of all contents of the hard drive

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A copy that includes all files and directories
texts.text: A copy that includes all files and directories

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. A bit-for-bit copy of all data
texts.text: A bit-for-bit copy of all data

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. An encrypted copy of all contents of the hard drive
texts.text: An encrypted copy of all contents of the hard drive

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: C is the correct answer.
texts.text: C is the correct answer.

texts.label: section_header
texts.orig: Justification:
texts.text: Justification:

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: A. Whether a copy is compressed is irrelevant, and a straight copy operation will not include everything on the hard disk that is not identified by the operating system as a standard file.
texts.text: Whether a copy is compressed is irrelevant, and a straight copy operation will not include everything on the hard disk that is not identified by the operating system as a standard file.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: B. A copy of all files and directories will not be an image of the hard disk and will fail to copy a variety of data, including data between the end of a file and the end of the disk sector ("slack space") and deleted files that have not been overwritten.
texts.text: A copy of all files and directories will not be an image of the hard disk and will fail to copy a variety of data, including data between the end of a file and the end of the disk sector ("slack space") and deleted files that have not been overwritten.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: C. There is no alternative to making a bit-for-bit copy. For legally sufficient evidence, only a bit copy will result in a true image of the hard drive.
texts.text: There is no alternative to making a bit-for-bit copy. For legally sufficient evidence, only a bit copy will result in a true image of the hard drive.

texts.label: list_item
texts.orig: D. Whether the data are encrypted is not relevant, and copying all files and folders will miss certain data such as data between the end of a file and the end of the disk sector (slack space).
texts.text: Whether the data are encrypted is not relevant, and copying all files and folders will miss certain data such as data between the end of a file and the end of the disk sector (slack space).
